Tumor Type: Primary or metastatic brain tumors (mixed. Breast ca, glioblastoma, low-grade glioma, chondrosarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, lung ca metastases)
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for tumor resection with peritumoral microdialysis catheter placement
Sample Size (n): 12 enrolled. 10 with dialysate samples (Cohort 1 n=6 surgery-only, Cohort 2 n=4 surgery+temsirolimus)
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Cohort 1 median 53 y (39-63). Cohort 2 median 52 y (31-70)
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: 17 cytokines/chemokines quantifiable in dialysate of at least 8/10 patients, namely IL-8, IP-10, MCP-1, MIP-1beta, IL-6, IL-12p40/70, IL-1RA, MIP-1alpha, RANTES, IFN-alpha, G-CSF, IL-2R, VEGF, IL-17, IL-10, MIG, IFN-gamma
Biomarker Biological Source: Inflammatory chemotactic cytokines released by tumor cells, glioma cells, immune cells, capillary endothelial cells, and injured neurons and astrocytes in the peritumoral microenvironment
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Interleukins and chemokines reflect a localized acute inflammatory response to tumor presence and surgical trauma. IL-6 activates JAK/STAT pathway in tumors, IL-8 regulates angiogenic activity in gliomas. MCP-1/IP-10 recruit monocytes and T cells
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Continuous dialysate sampling every 6h for 96h post craniotomy. Paired serum samples every 6h from patient 4 of cohort 1 onward. Baseline then 48h and 96h timepoints reported
Key Findings: Most cytokines/chemokines markedly elevated within 8h post op, declining significantly over 96h (11/17 cytokines with significant decreasing slope, p<0.05, namely IL-8, IP-10, MCP-1, MIP-1beta, IL-6, IL-12p40/70, MIP-1alpha, IFN-alpha, G-CSF, IL-2R, VEGF). Intracerebral levels several fold higher than serum for most cytokines. No significant temsirolimus effect detected. Reflects localized rather than systemic inflammatory response to tumor plus surgical trauma
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Tumor Type: Suspected diffuse glioma (WHO grade II-IV)
Surgical Procedure: Awake brain tumor surgery with intraoperative cortical/subcortical electrostimulation
Imaging Modality: Preoperative volumetric MRI (FLAIR/gadolinium T1) for tumor and extent of resection segmentation
Neuropsychological Tests: Cognitive screener, namely object naming, reading, attention span, working memory, inhibition, inhibition/switching, visuoperception, administered at 4 timepoints
Radiological Outcome Definition: Extent of resection defined radiologically from pre and post operative (within 72h) MRI volumetric segmentation
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Postoperative cognitive functioning defined as performance on the cognitive screener across seven domains
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Administered by a clinical neuropsychologist at 4 timepoints, namely pre op (mean 2.5 days before), intraoperative (26/37 patients), early post op (mean 1.6 days), late post op (weeks). Friedman ANOVA with Wilcoxon post hoc
Key Findings: Overall cognitive functioning stable across timepoints A-C-D except inhibition task reaction time (Friedman p=.005), significantly slower at early post op vs pre op (z=-2.85, p=.004), improving trend at late vs early (z=-2.38, p=.017), no difference pre vs late. Mean extent of resection 83.6+/-21.3%, lower for recurrent (71.3%) vs primary surgery (87.5%, p<.05)

Tumor Type: Left perisylvian glioma (grade II-IV. Glioblastoma 40%, astrocytoma 47%, oligodendroglioma 13%)
Surgical Procedure: Awake craniotomy with direct cortical stimulation language mapping and image guided resection
Imaging Modality: Resting state fMRI pre op (within 10d) and post op (within 6wk), graph theoretical analysis via Brain Connectivity Toolbox on AAL atlas
Neuropsychological Tests: Standardized battery by domain, namely attention, learning/memory (HVLT-R), processing speed, executive function, language, visuospatial, plus Clinical Trial Battery Composite (CTB COMP)
Radiological Outcome Definition: Graph theoretic connectomic properties, namely global/local efficiency, modularity, clustering coefficient, betweenness centrality, assortativity, compared pre to post op
Cognitive Outcome Definition: NCF change defined as pre to postoperative z score shift per test, categorized stable/improved/mild/moderate/severe decline
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Standard of care neuropsychological evaluation within 2 weeks pre op and again within 12 weeks post op before adjuvant therapy. Wilcoxon signed rank tests. Spearman correlation with connectomic metric change
Key Findings: 87% showed decline (z<=-1.00) on >=1 NCF measure, 53% on >=5 measures. Significant large effect decline in TMTB, Similarities, COWA, Token, TMTA, HVLT-R Rec, CTB composite (p=.005). Betweenness centrality and assortativity significantly reduced postoperatively (p=.031, p=.027). Reductions associated with better NCF outcomes (Spearman rho=-.51 to -.78)

Study Design: Prospective open-label dose-escalation pilot trial (Part I only opened)
Tumor Type: Supratentorial glioma, low grade, IDH-mutant predominant, no measurable enhancing disease
Surgical Procedure: None, pharmacologic BBB modulation study, not a resection
Sample Size (n): 7 (one patient per dose level, namely 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.7, 1.0, 1.4 mg regadenoson)
Imaging Modality: Dynamic contrast enhanced perfusion MRI (Extended Tofts Ktrans). Contrast enhanced T1 weighted digital subtraction maps
Radiological Outcome Definition: Primary endpoint Ktrans >0.04 min-1 in normal appearing white matter (10x assumed normal BBB value), assessed in a 2cm ROI contralateral to tumor
Key Findings: Primary endpoint NOT met at any dose (mean post treatment Ktrans in NAWM 1.13x10-3 min-1, well below threshold). T1 subtraction Z-score in NAWM increased 74.0% (SEM 22.4%, p=.0163). No dose dependent trend. Well tolerated, no adverse events. Study closed prematurely before Part II due to COVID-19 and NCI funding priority shift
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Study Design: Retrospective analysis of a prospectively collected cohort
Tumor Type: Intracranial neoplasm (benign 72.7%, malignant 27.3%)
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for brain tumor resection under general anesthesia, ICU admission post op
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Median 48 y (IQR 36-58). By frailty group, namely non-frail 42, pre-frail 53, frail 64
Sex Distribution: 265/659 male (40.2%). Non-frail 36.4% M, pre-frail 43.5% M, frail 70.8% M
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Modified Frailty Index (mFI), 11-variable index adapted from the Canadian Study of Health and Aging Frailty Index. Non-frail mFI=0 (60.4%), pre-frail mFI=1-2 (36.0%), frail mFI>=3 (3.6%)
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Postoperative delirium defined as CAM-ICU positive on postoperative day 1 and/or day 3
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: CAM-ICU administered between 08:00-10:00 on postoperative day 1 (ICU) and day 3 (ICU or ward). First assessment at least 12h after ICU admission. Day 2 not assessed
Key Findings: POD incidence 18.8% overall, rising with frailty status (non-frail 12.8%, pre-frail 27.0%, frail 37.5%, p<.001). Frailty independently associated with POD (adjusted OR 1.7, p=.032), longer length of stay (B=0.09, p=.007), and higher total costs (B=4.5, p=.036). Other independent POD risk factors, namely age, education, malignant tumor, frontal approach, bleeding, surgery duration, midazolam use, pain score
Evidence stream: Systemic frailty indices and perioperative risk

Tumor Type: Intracranial meningioma, WHO grade 1-3
Surgical Procedure: Meningioma resection (gross-total or subtotal)
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Not reported as single overall mean. Age entered as continuous covariate (OR per year 1.03, p=.001)
Sex Distribution: Not reported as single overall total in source text
Imaging Modality: Early postoperative MRI with B1000 DWI and ADC maps (<72h) for infarction detection. Classified rim, sector, combined, or remote, >=3mm cutoff
Radiological Outcome Definition: Postoperative infarction defined as high B1000 signal with corresponding low ADC value not explained by other diffusion abnormalities, minimum 3mm thickness, manually segmented
Neurological Deficit Definition: New neurological deficit defined as permanent paresis or permanent dysphasia/aphasia
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Registered at follow-up visits >=4 weeks after surgery, retrospectively retrieved from medical records. Fisher exact test vs infarction status
Cognitive Outcome Definition: QoL via EQ-5D-3L (mobility, self-care, activity, pain, anxiety, plus VAS) and EORTC QLQ-C30 plus BN20 (future uncertainty, visual impairment, motor dysfunction, communication)
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: EQ-5D-3L administered 1-3 days before surgery and 1 month post op via telephone interview. EORTC QLQ-C30/BN20 available only 2015 onward (n=141)
Key Findings: Infarctions in 114/327 (34.9%). Median volume 4.5 mL. Rim 37.7%, sector 38.6%, combined 21.9%, remote 1.8%. Permanent deficits in 22/327 (6.7%), strongly associated with infarction (72.7% of deficit patients had infarction, p<.001). Age associated with infarction risk (OR 1.03/year, p=.001). No significant HRQoL difference except more future uncertainty in infarction group (p=.048). Overall EQ-5D improved post surgery
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Tumor Type: Diffuse glioma, WHO grade 2-4, newly diagnosed or recurrent
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for glioma resection (primary or reoperation)
Sample Size (n): 539 operations (320 primary, 219 reoperations) from 579 consented of 769 eligible
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Reported only in age quartiles, namely Q1 18-44y, Q2 45-55y, Q3 56-64y, Q4 >=65y
Sex Distribution: Not reported as single overall total. Reported per infarction subgroup only
Imaging Modality: Early postoperative MRI with B1000 DWI/ADC (<72h). Tumor and infarction segmented and registered to MNI atlas (ANTs SyN) for heatmaps
Radiological Outcome Definition: Postoperative infarction defined as restricted diffusion (relative ADC <0.7x10^-3 mm2/s vs contralateral hemisphere), >=3mm diameter cutoff, classified rim/sector/combined/remote
Key Findings: Infarctions in 238/539 (44.2%). Rim 36%, sector 43%, combined 17%, remote 3%. Median volume 1.7 cm3. More common in temporal lobe tumors (50.7%, p=.017). Positive correlation with tumor volume (r=.267, p<.001) and intraoperative bleeding (r=.176, p=.014). Positive association with age (r=.193, p=.003). Infarction rate (32-72%) and volume differed significantly across surgeons (p=.037, p=.026)
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Tumor Type: Supratentorial tumors, namely pilocytic astrocytoma 29%, meningioma 23%, glioblastoma 20%, anaplastic astrocytoma 17%, oligodendroglioma 11%
Surgical Procedure: Elective surgical decompression/resection of supratentorial tumor under general anesthesia (isoflurane <1.0 MAC + N2O)
Imaging Modality: Preoperative CT/MRI used only to classify midline shift (>5mm) and peritumoral edema, not a primary outcome
Hemodynamic Measurements: Transcranial Doppler, namely Transient Hyperemic Response Ratio (THRR, autoregulation, via 10s carotid compression) and CO2 reactivity (via voluntary hyperventilation), tested pre op and 6-24h post op
Radiological Outcome Definition: THRR >1.1 defined normal autoregulation. CO2 reactivity defined as percent change in Vmca per mmHg decrease in PaCO2
Key Findings: Overall THRR intact and unchanged pre to post op (1.27 vs 1.30, p=.11). Autoregulation impaired pre operatively in 7/35 (20%) and remained impaired in all 7 post operatively (p<.001). Larger tumor size (median 100 vs 40 cm3, p=.002) and midline shift >5mm (100% vs 15%, p<.001) were risk factors. CO2 reactivity normal and unchanged in all patients (p=.07)
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Study Design: Cross-sectional case-control study (tumor tissue IHC paired with CSF cytokine analysis)
Tumor Type: High-grade glioma, namely IDH-wildtype GBM WHO IV (n=14), IDH-wildtype anaplastic astrocytoma WHO III (n=4)
Surgical Procedure: Tumor resection. Tissue and CSF sampled before radio/chemotherapy
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 63 y both GBM (range 31-79) and AA (range 45-85) groups. Controls mean 63 y
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: CSF 30-plex cytokine panel plus CXCL13 ELISA. IHC for CD45, CD68, CD163 in tumor core, infiltration zone, perivascular area
Biomarker Biological Source: CD45+ blood-derived leukocytes. CD68+ pan-macrophage/microglia. CD163+ M2-polarized macrophage subset. CSF cytokines from tumor and tumor-associated macrophages/microglia and other immune cells
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Low CD45+ indicates limited lymphocyte immunosurveillance. Predominant CD68+/CD163+ indicates macrophage-dominated pro-tumorigenic microenvironment. IL-7 reduction suggests impaired T-cell homeostasis. Negative macrophage correlation with several cytokines consistent with M2-polarizing milieu
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: CSF and tissue sampled once, at time of tumor resection, before radiotherapy or chemotherapy
Key Findings: CD68+ macrophages dominate infiltrate (19-27%) vs sparse CD45+ leukocytes (3-7%) (p<.01). CD163+ M2-macrophages 5-15%. Higher perivascular infiltration than tumor core (p=.008). IL-7 significantly downregulated in GBM CSF vs controls (p=.009). CD68+ infiltration significantly negatively correlated with eotaxin, IFN-gamma, IL-1beta, IL-2, IL-10, IL-13, IL-16, VEGF, and inflammatory cluster factor score (all p<.01)
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Tumor Type: Glioma, namely glioblastoma/gliosarcoma 73.5%, IDH-mutant grade II-III 17.6%, IDH-wildtype grade II-III 5.9%, grade I ganglioglioma 2.9%
Surgical Procedure: Glioma resection (craniotomy)
Imaging Modality: Pre and post op (<72h) MRI for ischemic lesion volume via ADC/DWI, correlated with biomarker levels
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Plasma GFAP, tau, and neurofilament light (NfL), measured by Simoa single-molecule array
Biomarker Biological Source: GFAP from astrocyte cytoskeleton. Tau from thin non-myelinated axons of cortical interneurons. NfL from large-caliber myelinated axons
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: GFAP marks astrocytic injury and can leak from glioma cells via disrupted BBB. Tau marks axonal/cortical interneuron injury. NfL marks large-axon injury with delayed second peak reflecting Wallerian degeneration
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Blood drawn at 6 timepoints, namely day before surgery, immediately after surgery, and postoperative days 1, 3, 5, 10
Radiological Outcome Definition: Postoperative ischemic lesion volume via ADC/DWI within 72h, correlated with biomarker levels
Biomarker Outcome Definition: Absolute plasma concentration at each postoperative timepoint and change from immediately preoperative baseline
Neurological Deficit Definition: New postoperative neurological deficit, transient or persistent at 30 days (binary outcome)
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Collected from patient records. Compared between deficit and no-deficit groups via Mann-Whitney U test against Day-1 biomarker levels
Key Findings: GFAP, tau, NfL all significantly increased Day 1 and 3 vs baseline (p<.001). NfL biphasic with later higher peak at Day 10 (p=.028). Day-1 levels and change from baseline correlated with ischemic lesion volume. Higher Day-1 GFAP (112.6 vs 36.3 ng/mL, p=.048) and NfL (86.2 vs 52.2 pg/mL, p=.043) in patients with new deficits. GFAP/NfL higher in GBM/GS vs IDH-mutant lower-grade glioma (p<.001)
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Tumor Type: Glioma of the left hemisphere in language and nonlanguage areas, untreated or recurrent
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for glioma resection near eloquent areas
Imaging Modality: 3D T1 and 2D T2 weighted MRI for tumor location and volume, pre op and within 72h post op
Neuropsychological Tests: Comprehensive protocol, namely language (AAT subtests, Boston Naming Test, category/letter fluency), memory (15 Words Test), attention/executive (TMTA, TMTB, TMTBA, Stroop I-III and interference), visuoconstruction (Clock Drawing Test)
Radiological Outcome Definition: Extent of resection calculated as pre operative minus post operative tumor volume from T2 weighted MRI segmentation
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Domain score defined as mean z score of tests within a domain, impairment defined as z score below -2
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Assessed 1-2 months pre operatively and 3-4 months post operatively. Compared to normative z scores and to each other with paired t tests or Wilcoxon
Key Findings: Patients worse than normal population pre and post op in language, memory, executive domains (p<.05). Significant postoperative decline in language domain (t=2.34, p=.027) and executive functions (t=2.45, p=.022). Language decline only in patients with tumor in/near language areas (t=2.33, p=.029). No effect of tumor volume, histology, grade, extent of resection, or adjuvant treatment

Tumor Type: Primary glioma, namely low-grade astrocytoma/oligodendroglioma (grade I), anaplastic astrocytoma (grade II), glioblastoma (grade III) per modified Ringertz classification
Surgical Procedure: None, preoperative imaging study only. 16/73 underwent biopsy alone for grading
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Brain tumor microenvironment. Neurovascular unit disruption
Imaging Modality: Dynamic susceptibility contrast enhanced perfusion MRI at 1.5T for rCBV and Ktrans via first-pass pharmacokinetic modeling, correlated with histopathologic grade
Radiological Outcome Definition: Maximal rCBV and maximal Ktrans measured in 4 ROIs per lesion, correlated with grade via Tukey HSD and Spearman/Pearson coefficients
Key Findings: rCBV significantly different across all three grades (p<.0005), strongly correlated with grade (Spearman r=.817). Ktrans differed only between grade I and grades II/III combined (p=.027), weaker correlation (Spearman r=.234). RCBV and Ktrans only modestly correlated (Spearman r=.266, not significant). Only rCBV significantly predicted high-grade glioma (p<.0001), Ktrans did not (p=.07)
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Tumor Type: Treatment-naive glioma WHO grade I-IV and meningioma (including one hemangiopericytoma)
Surgical Procedure: Gross total or subtotal resection within 2 days after MRI, imaging performed preoperatively
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Brain tumor microenvironment. Neurovascular unit disruption
Imaging Modality: Steady-state T1 weighted (ssT1) and first-pass T2 weighted (fpT2*) dynamic contrast enhanced MRI for Ktrans, plus fpT2* rCBV, correlated with blinded pathologist grade
Radiological Outcome Definition: Ktrans from ssT1 vs fpT2* methods correlated with each other and with grade using Kruskal-Wallis, Wilcoxon rank sum, Pearson correlation with Fisher Z transformation
Key Findings: All three variables (rCBV, ssT1 Ktrans, fpT2* Ktrans) differed across glioma grades II-IV (p=.03, .006, .003). Only Ktrans (both methods) differentiated grade IV from lower grade after Bonferroni correction. FpT2* Ktrans highly predictive of ssT1 Ktrans in gliomas (Pearson r=.95, p<.001) but not meningiomas (Pearson r=.16, p=.74), attributed to extreme vascular leakiness violating model assumptions
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Tumor Type: Low-grade glioma WHO grade II, no adjuvant therapy
Surgical Procedure: Resective surgery for LGG
Sample Size (n): 10 (8 with complete pre and post neuropsychological data)
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Not reported as single mean. Individual ages 18-53 listed
Imaging Modality: Magnetoencephalography (306-channel) eyes-closed resting state, source reconstructed to AAL atlas via beamformer, pre op and within 6 months post op (mean 16 weeks)
Neuropsychological Tests: Six cognitive domains, namely executive functioning, psychomotor speed, verbal memory, attention, working memory, information processing, converted to z scores
Radiological Outcome Definition: Extent of resection computed from pre and post operative tumor volumes using iPlan software
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Cognitive domain change defined as delta z score (pre minus post) per domain per patient
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Assessed at same two timepoints as MEG. Wilcoxon signed rank tests. Correlated with PLI connectivity change via Kendall tau
Key Findings: No group-level cognitive difference pre to post surgery in any domain. Default mode network connectivity in lower alpha band increased after resection (p=.006), right frontoparietal network connectivity increased in upper alpha band (p=.003). DMN increase correlated with improved verbal memory (tau=.571, p=.048). Right FPN increase correlated with improved attention (tau=.857, p=.003), working memory, and executive functioning

Tumor Type: Supratentorial meningioma
Surgical Procedure: Elective meningioma resection
Imaging Modality: Preoperative MRI (T1, T2, T1+Gd, FLAIR) and postoperative CT at 36-48h for tumor/edema/bleeding volume and midline shift via BrainSCAN software
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum S100 beta, sampled on admission and immediately, 24h and 48h after surgery, measured with Roche Elecsys S100 assay
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Biological half-life about 30 minutes. Persistent elevation indicates continuous astrocytic damage or blood-brain barrier dysfunction
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Serum sampled at 4 fixed timepoints, namely preoperative baseline, immediately post op, 24h post op, 48h post op
Radiological Outcome Definition: Tumor volume, edema volume, bleeding volume and midline shift on BrainSCAN volumetric analysis of pre op MRI and post op CT
Biomarker Outcome Definition: Serum S100 beta concentration at each timepoint and correlation with radiological/clinical findings
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Cognitive outcome via Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE) score change from pre to 48h post op
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: MMSE administered pre operatively and 48h post operatively. Deterioration defined as any decrease
Key Findings: Preoperative S100 beta did not correlate with tumor/edema volume. Rose significantly from baseline 0.065 to 0.138/0.142/0.155 microg/L at immediate/24h/48h (p<.0001). Higher immediate levels with difficult surgical plane (p=.01). Higher 24h/48h levels with CT bleeding (p=.046/.034) and midline shift (p=.005/.006). MMSE deterioration correlated with S100 beta elevation at all timepoints (p=.005, .011, .036)
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Study Design: Retrospective cohort study using ACS NSQIP database
Tumor Type: Meningioma, intrinsic brain tumor, metastatic disease, other cranial tumors
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for tumor resection
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Not reported as single overall mean. Reported per frailty subgroup
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: 5-factor modified Frailty Index (mFI-5), namely congestive heart failure, COPD, dependent functional status, diabetes, hypertension. Classified no frailty (0), low frailty (0.2), medium-to-high frailty (>0.2)
Neurological Deficit Definition: Major complication defined as one or more of deep/organ-space SSI, wound disruption, pneumonia, sepsis, unplanned intubation, PE, prolonged ventilation, renal failure, stroke with deficit, coma, nerve injury, cardiac arrest, MI, graft/flap failure within 30 days
Key Findings: Low frailty (30.7%) and medium-to-high frailty (10.6%) both independently associated with increased major complication (adjusted OR 1.41 and 1.61), non-home discharge (OR 1.32 and 1.80), 30-day readmission (OR 1.29 and 1.39), and 30-day mortality (OR 1.87 and 2.42), all p<.001, adjusted for age, sex, BMI, ASA class, smoking, dyspnea, weight loss, steroid use, bleeding disorder, tumor type, operative time
Evidence stream: Systemic frailty indices and perioperative risk

Tumor Type: Brain tumor of any type scheduled for elective resection
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for brain tumor resection
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Nonfrail mean 50.1 y, moderately frail mean 56.1 y, frail mean 61.36 y
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Hopkins Frailty Score (HFS), namely shrinking, exhaustion, low activity, weakness (dynamometry), slowed walking speed. Classified nonfrail (0-1), moderately frail (2-3), frail (4-5), moderate+frail combined for analysis (25.4% of cohort)
Neurological Deficit Definition: Postoperative complication defined as pneumonia, UTI, DVT, PE, new neurologic deficit, CSF leak, wound dehiscence/infection within 30 days including mortality
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: New neurologic deficit defined as any new deficit within 30 days, obtained from medical record review, compared by chi-square between frail and nonfrail groups
Key Findings: Frail patients had 10.36-fold higher odds of non-home discharge (95% CI 3.6-30.1), 2.09-fold higher odds of any postoperative complication (95% CI 1.09-3.98), 1.66-fold higher odds of longer length of stay (95% CI 1.24-2.21), independent of ASA/Lee/Eagle score and age. Slowed walking speed was the HFS component most predictive of complications (p=.006)
Evidence stream: Systemic frailty indices and perioperative risk

Tumor Type: Diffuse glioma primarily of frontal and parietal regions
Surgical Procedure: Resection of diffuse glioma, mostly with cortical mapping given eloquent locations
Sex Distribution: Not stated as single ratio. Individual sex listed per patient (predominantly male)
Imaging Modality: Resting-state and task-based (n-back) fMRI pre op, patient-specific fronto-parietal network (FPN) ROIs from n-back activation, connectivity via Pearson correlation of residual BOLD time series
Neuropsychological Tests: NIH Toolbox Cognitive Battery (NIHTB-CB), 7 subtests yielding fluid, crystallized, and overall composite T scores
Radiological Outcome Definition: Extent of resection computed from pre and post operative tumor volume on Myrian software
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Cognitive outcome defined as change in NIHTB-CB composite, fluid, and crystallized T scores from pre op to one month post op
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: NIHTB-CB administered within 2 weeks pre op and about one month (mean 32.4 days) post op. Correlated with FPN connectivity via Spearman rank correlation
Key Findings: Average FPN connectivity inversely correlated with preoperative composite cognitive score (p=.024). Tumor-hemisphere parietal connectivity inversely correlated with composite (p=.023) and fluid cognition (p=.025) but not crystallized cognition. Non-tumor hemisphere parietal connectivity predicted change in composite (p=.009) and fluid score (p=.019) at one month, tumor-hemisphere connectivity did not (p=.086)

Tumor Type: Glioma (low and high grade, non-contrast-enhancing at diagnosis) in eloquent areas
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for glioma resection near eloquent areas
Imaging Modality: 3D T1 and 2D T2 weighted MRI pre op and at 3 months and 1 year post op, manual T2 delineation for extent of resection
Neuropsychological Tests: Same protocol as Satoer 2012, namely language (AAT, BNT, fluency), memory (15 Words Test), attention/executive (TMTA, TMTB, TMTBA), at three timepoints
Radiological Outcome Definition: Extent of resection categorized as biopsy (<20%), partial (20-89%), subtotal (90-99%), total (100%)
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Cognitive change score defined as difference between test scores at consecutive timepoints
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Administered pre op (mean 1.4 months before), 3 months, and 1 year post op. Paired t tests or Wilcoxon signed rank across timepoints
Key Findings: Impairments present pre and post op in language, memory, attention, executive domains (p<.05). Permanent decline in category fluency (p=.030) while letter fluency and naming improved between 3 months and 1 year (p=.047, p=.026). Verbal recall improved short-term and remained stable. TMTA/TMTB normalized by 1 year. No effect of grade, localization, extent of resection, or adjuvant treatment on change scores

Tumor Type: Diffuse glioma WHO grade II-IV (141 high grade, 41 low grade)
Surgical Procedure: Primary surgical resection under general anesthesia for diffuse glioma
Age (mean/median, range or SD): LGG median 39 y range 18-69. HGG median 61 y range 28-80
Imaging Modality: Preoperative (within 72h) and postoperative (within 48h) MRI for semi-automatic tumor volume segmentation via 3D Slicer and BrainVoyager
Cognitive Outcome Definition: EORTC QLQ-C30 cognitive functioning subscale, two items on memory and concentration scored 0-100, MCID of +/-10 used to classify improvement/stable/deterioration
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Self-administered questionnaire 1-3 days pre op, structured telephone interview at ~1 month and 6 months post op. Group-level t tests and mixed binomial regression. Individual predictors via binomial logistic regression
Key Findings: HGG mean cognitive score improved significantly from 70.9 pre op to 85.1 at 1 month and 83.3 at 6 months (p<.001). LGG remained stable around 80-81. Females scored lower than males. At individual level both improvement and deterioration frequently reported in both groups. Preoperative corticosteroid use and larger tumor volume independently predicted improvement at 1 month (OR 3.01 for steroids) but no predictors identified for 6-month improvement or deterioration at either timepoint

Tumor Type: Supratentorial low or high grade glioma in motor eloquent areas, newly diagnosed or recurrent
Surgical Procedure: Glioma resection with intraoperative motor evoked potential (MEP) monitoring
Imaging Modality: Early postoperative (within 48h) 3T MRI with DWI and ADC mapping, ischemic lesions classified as arterial territorial, terminal branch, or other/venous infarction
Radiological Outcome Definition: Ischemic lesion defined as DWI hyperintensity with corresponding ADC hypointensity, excluding methemoglobin related diffusion restriction on T2 gradient echo
Neurological Deficit Definition: New postoperative decline of motor function due to surgery, transient or permanent
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Intraoperative MEP amplitude decline of more than 50 percent from baseline defined as significant deterioration, classified reversible or irreversible, correlated with postoperative clinical motor exam and DWI findings blinded to IOM course
Key Findings: MEP amplitude decline over 50 percent observed in 21/70 (30 percent), of whom 76 percent had ischemic lesions on MRI versus 33 percent of patients without decline (p less than 0.05). Ischemic lesions found in 32/70 (46 percent) overall. Permanent motor deficit in 10/70 (14 percent), transient in 13 (19 percent). 8 of 10 permanent deficit patients had irreversible MEP loss, 2 had reversible MEP but still developed ischemic lesions (secondary ischemia not detectable intraoperatively). Ischemic events were the presumed cause of 7/10 (70 percent) permanent deficits, of which 5/7 (71 percent) were detected intraoperatively by MEP. Prior radiotherapy and tumor proximity to central arteries were risk factors for ischemia
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Tumor Type: Newly diagnosed or recurrent supratentorial low or high grade glioma
Surgical Procedure: Glioma resection (109 operations in 100 patients, 84 newly diagnosed, 25 recurrent)
Imaging Modality: Early postoperative (within 48h) 3T MRI with DWI and ADC mapping, ischemic lesions classified arterial territorial, terminal branch, or venous infarction using an angiographic vascular territory atlas
Radiological Outcome Definition: Ischemic lesion defined as focal DWI hyperintensity with corresponding ADC hypointensity, excluding methemoglobin related and thin resection border rim changes
Neurological Deficit Definition: New transient or permanent postoperative neurological deficit or worsening of neurological symptoms
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Prospectively documented clinical data, compared between ischemic lesion and no lesion groups using Pearson chi square test
Key Findings: New postoperative ischemic lesions in 26/84 (31 percent) newly diagnosed versus 20/25 (80 percent) recurrent gliomas (p less than 0.01). Permanent deficit in 6/84 (7 percent) newly diagnosed versus 4/25 (16 percent) recurrent. Ischemic lesions more common in tumors involving central artery territories (43 percent vs 21 percent, p less than 0.05). No significant effect of age, tumor grade, or number of affected lobes on ischemia incidence. New neurological deficits significantly more frequent in patients with ischemic lesions than without (p less than 0.05)
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Tumor Type: Newly diagnosed suspiciously malignant CNS lesion planned for complete resection, 25 glioma and 7 brain metastases
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy and resection of intracerebral tumor
Imaging Modality: Postoperative MRI within 72h for residual tumor volume via BrainLab iplan software based on pre and postoperative contrast enhanced T1 imaging
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum glial fibrillary acidic protein (sGFAP), measured by electrochemiluminometric immunoassay (Elecsys GFAP prototype), sampled preoperatively, at ICU admission on day of surgery, and postoperative days 1, 3, and 7
Biomarker Biological Source: GFAP is the major intermediate filament protein of normal and reactive astrocytes, and is also expressed by glial origin brain tumors including glioblastoma
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Elevated postoperative sGFAP reflects astroglial damage from surgical trauma and, in glioma, additional release from GFAP-positive tumor cells. Preoperative levels help distinguish glial from non-glial (metastatic) lesions
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Five fixed timepoints, namely day before surgery (baseline), ICU admission on day of surgery, postoperative day 1, day 3, and day 7
Radiological Outcome Definition: Postoperative residual tumor volume assessed on MRI within 72h using BrainLab iplan volumetric software
Biomarker Outcome Definition: Serum GFAP concentration at each of the five timepoints and its correlation with residual tumor volume
Key Findings: Preoperative sGFAP significantly higher in glioma than brain metastasis (0.18 vs 0.08 microgram per liter, p=.0198). GBM sGFAP significantly increased after surgery (p=.0172) peaking at postoperative day 1 (mean 1.423 microgram per liter) and still above baseline at day 7. Brain metastasis sGFAP also rose and peaked at day 1 but with generally lower levels than glioma. ROC analysis gave a diagnostic cutoff of 0.135 microgram per liter distinguishing GBM from metastasis preoperatively with 70 percent accuracy (AUC 0.74). Postoperative sGFAP did not correlate with residual tumor volume on day 3 or day 7 (p=.5151 and p=.2500), so sGFAP was not suitable as a marker of residual glioma tissue
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Tumor Type: Supratentorial meningioma (frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital, suprasellar)
Surgical Procedure: Meningioma resection
Imaging Modality: CT/MRI for tumor volume and peritumoral edema volume via prolate ellipse formula (length times depth times width times 0.523)
Neuropsychological Tests: Battery covering mental speed (digit symbol substitution), focused attention (color trail test 1), sustained attention (digit vigilance test), verbal fluency (COWAT), category fluency (animal names), verbal and visual working memory (N-back), verbal memory (RAVLT), visuospatial ability and visual memory (Rey complex figure test), compared to normative data from 540 Indian subjects (NIMHANS battery)
Radiological Outcome Definition: Tumor volume and peritumoral edema volume calculated from maximal diameters on MRI using the prolate ellipse formula. Presence of raised intracranial pressure assessed clinically
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Impairment defined as a score at least 1 standard deviation below the age, gender, and education matched normative mean (approximately 15th percentile). Overall cognitive status considered impaired if impaired on at least one test
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Administered by a neurosurgeon and psychologist just before surgery and again 3 months after surgery, compared to matched normative data and to each patient's own preoperative score using Wilcoxon signed rank, Mann-Whitney U, chi square, ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis tests
Key Findings: 73.7 percent of patients had impairment on at least one cognitive test preoperatively, most commonly memory (57.9 percent) and attention/executive functions (54.4 percent). Frontal and temporal tumor groups had the highest impairment frequency (90 percent each). Raised intracranial pressure associated with significantly more impairment (95.2 percent vs 61.1 percent, p=.005). Tumor volume greater than 35cc and peritumoral edema greater than 40cc were associated with more deficits, particularly in the frontal group. Postoperatively there was significant improvement in nearly all cognitive functions among patients with preoperative impairment (p less than 0.05 for most tests except sustained attention), with the improvement statistically significant specifically in the frontal and temporal groups. No cognitive deterioration was observed in any subgroup

Tumor Type: Brain tumor, namely meningioma, high grade glioma, pituitary tumor, brain metastasis, vestibular schwannoma, low grade glioma, other
Surgical Procedure: Primary surgery for brain tumor
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: 5 factor modified Frailty Index (mFI-5), namely functional status, diabetes, COPD, congestive heart failure, hypertension requiring medication. Classified zero frailty (mFI=0, 43 percent), some frailty (mFI=1, 38 percent), significant frailty (mFI at least 2, 19 percent)
Key Findings: Mean ICU and total length of stay were 1.69 and 5.24 days. Each additional point on the mFI-5 was independently associated with a 0.32 day increase in ICU LOS (p=.007) and 1.38 day increase in total LOS (p less than .001) on multivariate analysis adjusted for age, sex, race, ethnicity, ASA class and diagnosis. Increasing mFI-5 also independently predicted greater odds of pulmonary embolism/DVT (OR 1.50), physiological/metabolic derangement (OR 3.66), respiratory failure (OR 1.55), and sepsis (OR 2.12), all p less than .05. Total and imaging charges increased by 5846 and 416 dollars respectively per mFI-5 point (p less than .001). MFI-5 was not a significant independent predictor of 30 day readmission (OR 1.24, p=.080)
Evidence stream: Systemic frailty indices and perioperative risk

Study Design: Prospective cohort study with matched healthy control comparison
Tumor Type: Unifocal frontal meningioma, histologically benign
Surgical Procedure: Total surgical removal of frontal meningioma
Sex Distribution: 37F/17M in both patient and control groups (matched)
Imaging Modality: 1.5T triplanar MRI (T1, T2, contrast enhanced T1) for tumor volumetry using neuronavigation software
Neuropsychological Tests: Extensive battery, namely verbal and figural memory (Wechsler Memory Scale Revised), attention (tonic/phasic alertness, divided attention, flexibility via computerized tests), processing speed and shifting (Trail Making Test A/B), executive function (verbal and figural fluency), visuoconstructive ability (Complex Figure Test copy). WIP short form WAIS for IQ measured preoperatively only
Radiological Outcome Definition: Tumor volume via neuronavigation software volumetry. Peritumoral edema classified none, in vicinity, or widespread per Trittmacher criteria. Brain compression classified none, unilateral, or bilateral
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Ipsative scores computed as preoperative minus postoperative test score, representing individual cognitive change. Compared against matched healthy volunteers tested twice at the same interval to control for practice effects
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Assessed 2-3 days preoperatively and 4-9 months postoperatively (same interval used for the twice-tested control group). Wilcoxon, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Study had 73 percent power to detect a medium effect size at alpha .05
Key Findings: Preoperatively patients were significantly impaired versus controls in working memory, fluency, tonic alertness, processing speed, shifting, divided attention, and flexibility (p less than .05), but not in memory or visuoconstructive ability. Postoperatively no cognitive domain showed deterioration, while attentional functions (tonic alertness, divided attention, flexibility, shifting), processing speed, and immediate figural recall improved significantly. Lesion size, edema, brain compression, and preoperative seizures had only minor influence on outcome. Lateralization and localization influenced the pattern of recovery, with right frontal and frontobasal tumors showing the broadest postoperative improvement in attentional functions

Study Design: Retrospective cohort study with survival analysis on archival tumor tissue
Tumor Type: Diffusely infiltrating astrocytoma WHO grade II to IV (diagnosed 1999-2006)
Surgical Procedure: Partial (47 patients) or complete (50 patients) tumor resection followed by radiotherapy in most cases (not the primary focus of the study)
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Immunohistochemistry for IL-6, IL-8, VEGF and phosphorylated (activated) STAT-3 on archival paraffin embedded tumor tissue. CD34 immunostaining for microvessel density and morphometry
Biomarker Biological Source: IL-6 and IL-8 (Th2 cytokines) expressed by neoplastic astrocytoma cells, particularly perinecrotic pseudopalisading cells, and by perivascular inflammatory and endothelial cells. Phospho-STAT-3 is a nuclear transcription factor activated downstream of cytokine and growth factor signaling in neoplastic cell nuclei
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: IL-8, IL-6, VEGF and p-STAT-3 expression correlate with tumor grade and degree of necrosis, reflecting hypoxia driven angiogenic and inflammatory signaling in the tumor microenvironment. IL-8 independently predicted worse survival while p-STAT-3 predicted improved survival in high grade tumors, suggesting a dual, context dependent oncogenic and tumor suppressive role for STAT-3 signaling
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Single measurement on archival primary tumor tissue obtained at diagnosis, prior to radiotherapy
Key Findings: IL-8 and IL-6 expression increased with tumor grade and degree of necrosis (p less than .05). IL-8 positively correlated with p-STAT-3 (r=.332, p=.0013) and VEGF (r=.475, p less than .0001). IL-8 and p-STAT-3 both positively correlated with microvessel density (r=.481 and r=.207 respectively). On univariate survival analysis increased IL-8 and IL-6 expression adversely affected survival in the whole cohort (p=.0062 and p=.0109) while increased p-STAT-3 predicted improved survival specifically in grade III/IV tumors (p=.0032). On multivariate analysis only IL-8 expression retained independent prognostic significance (p=.043) alongside histologic grade
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Tumor Type: Meningioma (all sites, 96 percent histologically benign WHO grade I-II)
Surgical Procedure: Meningioma resection (total or subtotal)
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum S100B protein, measured by two site immunoluminometric assay (LIAISON-Sangtec 100), sampled preoperatively and daily for 7 consecutive postoperative days
Biomarker Biological Source: Astrocyte and glial cell derived calcium binding protein, present in the cytosol of glial and Schwann cells
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Elevated or persistently rising S100B indicates ongoing organic brain damage such as evolving edema, ischemia, or hematoma. The protein's short serum half life makes it a sensitive marker of acute secondary postoperative injury rather than chronic tumor related change
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Preoperative sample plus daily samples for 7 consecutive postoperative days. Area under the curve calculated over the first 144 postoperative hours
Radiological Outcome Definition: Postoperative CT documenting surgical hematoma with shift, ischemia/edema, or pneumocephalus, interpreted by neurologists blinded to S100B results
Biomarker Outcome Definition: First postoperative S100B value and 144 hour area under the curve, analyzed continuously and against a predefined cutoff of 0.4 microgram per liter
Neurological Deficit Definition: Postcraniotomy neurologic deterioration defined as definitive worsening of preexisting neurologic signs or new signs including deterioration in consciousness, mono or hemiparesis, aphasia, seizures, or death
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Clinical assessment plus serial postoperative CT scans (at least two scans if deterioration occurred). 6 month Glasgow Outcome Scale used for long term outcome
Key Findings: 50 percent of patients developed early postoperative neurologic deterioration and 30 percent had an unfavorable 6 month outcome. First postoperative S100B was significantly higher in patients with larger tumors, non-convexity sites, intraoperative technical difficulties, postoperative deterioration, and unfavorable outcome (all p less than .05). S100B above 0.4 microgram per liter carried a 9 fold higher risk of neurologic deterioration (relative risk 9.0, 95 percent CI 2.4-34, p less than .0001) and an 11 fold higher risk of poor 6 month outcome (relative risk 11, 95 percent CI 1.6-77, p=.002). The 144 hour area under the curve for S100B was the single most significant independent predictor of postoperative deterioration on multivariate logistic regression (p=.0013). ROC area under the curve was 0.80 for deterioration and 0.77 for 6 month outcome
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Study Design: Prospective ultrastructural (electron microscopy) case series, not a clinical outcome study
Tumor Type: Primary glial tumors, namely 1 anaplastic glioma, 2 malignant oligodendroglioma, 10 glioblastoma multiforme
Surgical Procedure: Lobectomy for tumor removal, with peritumoral and distant normal white matter sampled intraoperatively for electron microscopy
Sample Size (n): 13 patients (259 microvessel profiles analyzed, namely 75 normal, 184 peritumoral)
Key Findings: Peritumoral microvessels showed elongated junctional clefts (cleft index) and increased endothelial vesicle density compared with normal white matter vessels (p less than .02 to .03). Cleft index correlated positively with local tumor cell nuclear density (r=.62, p less than .05). The subset of vessels directly enveloped by tumor cells (18 percent of vessels examined) were the most abnormal, with thicker walls, larger pericytes, and higher cleft index than normal (p less than .01-.02), while vessels not directly enveloped by tumor were still mildly abnormal relative to normal brain. No fenestrae were observed in any peritumoral vessel. Occasional frank breaks in the vessel wall with red cell extravasation were seen. The findings support a contact-independent, concentration-dependent inductive effect of tumor derived factors on peritumoral vessel permeability, providing a structural blood-brain-barrier basis for tumor associated vasogenic edema
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Study Design: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
Tumor Type: Mixed intracranial tumors, namely meningioma, high grade glioma (WHO III-IV), low grade glioma (WHO I-II), metastasis, vestibular schwannoma, hemangioblastoma, lymphoma, epidermoid cyst (pituitary adenomas excluded)
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for tumor resection
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 56.6 y SD13.9 (range 18.6-80.3). Females 56.6 SD14.4, males 56.7 SD13.2
Neuropsychological Tests: NeuroCogFX computer based screening battery, 8 subtests, namely Digit Span (verbal short term memory), 2-Back (working memory), Simple Reaction (alertness), Go/NoGo (selective attention), Inverted Go/NoGo (selective attention and cognitive flexibility), Verbal Memory (verbal learning and recognition), Figural Memory (figural learning and recognition), Phonematic Fluency (phonemic literal word fluency). Mean test duration about 25 minutes
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Individual subtest and overall scores expressed as percentile ranks against normative data from 242 healthy individuals, categorized very poor (PR=0), poor (PR less than 3), marginal (PR less than 16), normal (PR 16-84), very good (PR greater than 84). Impaired defined as PR less than 16 (marginal, poor, or very poor). Overall score standardized to mean 100, SD 10. Pre to postoperative change categorized as no change, improvement, or decline
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Administered 1-2 days before craniotomy and again at first postoperative follow up 3-4 months after surgery, before radiotherapy or chemotherapy effects would be expected. Group comparisons via chi square or Fisher exact test, pre to postoperative change via McNemar test, no correction for multiple testing as an exploratory analysis
Key Findings: Significant postoperative improvement across the whole cohort was seen in the Go/noGo test (not impaired 59 percent preoperatively vs 72 percent at follow up, p=.003) and the figural memory test (67 percent vs 86 percent, p less than .001), with no significant decline in any of the eight subtests. The meningioma subgroup showed a significant improvement in overall standardized score from 93 to 98 (p=.001), while high grade glioma, low grade glioma, and metastasis subgroups showed no significant overall score change. Patients with malignant diagnoses (high grade glioma and metastasis) scored significantly lower preoperatively than those with more favorable diagnoses. Tumor location was not significantly associated with impairment pattern except that left temporal tumors showed worse preoperative Go/noGo performance (p=.022) and right hemisphere tumors showed worse postoperative figural memory performance (p=.011). Right frontal tumor location showed a significant overall score improvement from 90 to 94 (p=.037)

Study Design: Single center cross sectional retrospective survey, 1 year enrollment period
Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumors, namely meningioma, glioma, pituitary adenoma, and others including peripheral nerve tumor and craniopharyngioma
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for brain tumor resection under general or awake anesthesia, biopsy and ventriculoperitoneal shunt cases excluded
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 47.1 y SD14.28 in non delirium group vs 51.9 y SD12.66 in delirium group, overall range 14-80
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: National Institutes of Health type functional scoring not used, Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale used to classify delirium motor subtype
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Diagnosed with the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit and the standard Confusion Assessment Method, primary outcome was incidence within 72 hours after waking from anesthesia, subtype classified as hyperactive, hypoactive or mixed using the Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Screened every nursing shift by a trained research nurse from waking until 72 hours postoperatively or until discharge or death
Key Findings: Overall postoperative delirium incidence was 14.78 percent, hyperactive subtype 50.76 percent, hypoactive 41.67 percent, mixed 7.57 percent. Univariate risk factors included age over 50 years, male sex, tobacco use history, physical restraint, electrolyte disturbance, fever over 38.5C, longer duration of anesthesia and operation, glioma diagnosis, while pituitary adenoma and saddle area or subtentorial location were protective. The final stepwise multivariable model retained physical restraint, age over 50, longer duration of operation, electrolyte disturbance and tobacco use as independent predictors, with meningioma protective relative to other diagnoses, area under the curve 0.787. Delirium was associated with longer intensive care and hospital stay and higher hospitalization cost

Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumors, predominantly malignant glioma and metastasis, supratentorial in 90 percent of cases
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for tumor resection, biopsies excluded
Imaging Modality: Diffusion weighted MRI performed preoperatively and within 72 hours postoperatively, single shot multislice spin echo echo planar sequence
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale and Karnofsky Performance Scale used to grade deficits and functional status
Radiological Outcome Definition: Positive postoperative DWI defined as hyperintense signal extending beyond the tumor cavity margin without a corresponding T2 bright signal and without restricted diffusion on the preoperative scan, distinguished from a thin normal pericavity rim
Neurological Deficit Definition: New or worsened postoperative deficit defined as at least a one point increase on the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Complete neurological examination preoperatively, within 24 hours, at postoperative day 7, and at postoperative day 30 by chart review
Key Findings: 24 of 80 patients (30 percent) had a new or increased postoperative deficit. 15 of 80 (19 percent) had a positive postoperative DWI. Presence of a preoperative neurological deficit was the only significant multivariable predictor of new or increased postoperative deficit (odds ratio 3.9, p=.04), while falcine herniation was significant only in univariable analysis. A new DWI lesion was the only significant multivariable predictor of incomplete neurological recovery at day 7 and day 30 (odds ratio 0.03 and 0.04 respectively, both p=.005), corresponding to roughly 33 fold and 25 fold increased likelihood of incomplete recovery. Prior craniotomy and prior radiotherapy were significant only in univariable analyses for incomplete recovery. Tumor volume, histology, extent of resection and cardiovascular risk factors were not significant predictors
PMID/DOI Link: Neurosurgery 2006;58:60-66 (article DOI not resolvable from source text)
Evidence stream: Perioperative brain injury, imaging, and biomarkers

Study Design: Prospective mechanistic biomarker study on stereotactic biopsy specimens
Tumor Type: Glioblastoma (7), anaplastic astrocytoma (1), low grade astrocytoma (2), pilocytic astrocytoma (1), primary cerebral lymphoma (3)
Surgical Procedure: Stereotactic biopsy, not resection
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Not aggregated in source text, individual patient ages ranged approximately 25-73 y
Sex Distribution: Mixed, individual counts not aggregated in source text
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Brain tumor microenvironment. Neurovascular unit disruption
Imaging Modality: Dynamic two compartment computed tomography method quantifying blood to brain transport rate constant and plasma vascular volume at the biopsy site
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: VEGF messenger RNA by semiquantitative RT-PCR, VEGF protein by immunohistochemistry using monoclonal antibody A.4.6.1 and polyclonal antibody A.20
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: VEGF acts as an endothelial cell specific mitogen and potent inducer of vascular permeability, thought to mediate tumor angiogenesis and peritumoral vasogenic edema
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Single timepoint at stereotactic biopsy, not perioperative pre/post comparison
Key Findings: VEGF mRNA levels correlated significantly with the capillary permeability constant (r=0.667, p=.015) and with plasma vascular volume (r=0.778, p=.0017) in glial tumors. Glioblastomas showed the strongest VEGF upregulation and immunoreactivity. The three primary cerebral lymphomas had high permeability and vascular volume values but only modest VEGF upregulation, suggesting factors other than VEGF drive their vascular leakiness. VEGF protein localized predominantly to tumor vasculature on immunostaining
Evidence stream: Tumor biology, microenvironment, and blood-brain barrier

Tumor Type: Glioma, 49 percent low grade and 51 percent high grade (WHO grade I 26 percent, II 23 percent, III 30 percent, IV 21 percent)
Surgical Procedure: Awake craniotomy (sleep-awake-sleep technique) for tumor resection
Imaging Modality: T1 weighted with and without gadolinium and FLAIR MRI, lesion segmentation with voxel based topography reduced via principal component analysis
Neuropsychological Tests: Esame Neuropsicologico Breve 2 battery, 16 tests covering digit span, immediate and delayed prose memory, interference memory, trail making test A and B, token test, phonemic fluency, abstract reasoning, cognitive estimation, overlapping figures, drawing tasks, clock drawing, and praxis tests
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Delta Z score, one week postoperative minus preoperative, z scored against 370 age matched healthy controls per test. Clinically relevant decline defined as a within patient drop of at least 1 standard deviation
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Full battery administered before surgery and approximately 1 week after surgery
Key Findings: 85 percent of test scores across the sample were stable or improved one week after surgery, with significant group level decline only for trail making test A, verbal fluency and overlapping figures. Presurgical cognitive performance was the strongest predictor of early postsurgical cognitive scores and significantly improved prediction beyond demographics alone, while tumor volume, grading and lesion topography did not significantly improve prediction once presurgical cognition was included. A model using demographics plus presurgical cognition achieved a leave one out actual to predicted correlation of r=0.57

Tumor Type: Right frontal IDH mutated glioma, WHO grade II 70 percent, III 20 percent, IV 10 percent
Surgical Procedure: Awake craniotomy with continuous intraoperative direct electrical stimulation mapping and tumor resection
Sample Size (n): 20 surgical cases in 18 patients, including 5 redo surgeries
Imaging Modality: 3D T1 MRI for surgical cavity segmentation registered to MNI template, language fMRI performed in a subset to confirm left hemisphere language lateralization
Neuropsychological Tests: Battery covering language and semantic cognition (picture naming, complex language tasks, reading and writing, metaphor comprehension, categorical and literal fluency, nonverbal semantic association), attention and executive function (digit span, PASAT, trail making test, Stroop, d2 attention test, Rey figure copy), visuospatial cognition (line bisection, Bells and Clock tests), memory (delayed Rey figure, RI-RL16), and social cognition (Reading the Mind in the Eyes, facial emotion recognition, faux pas recognition)
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Domain z scores. Long term impairment in a domain defined as at least one test z score decreasing by 1.5 units or more relative to the preoperative baseline
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Assessed just before surgery, immediately (within one week) after surgery, and again 4 months after surgery
Key Findings: Preoperatively, mild deficits were present in 45 percent of cases, mainly executive function, attention and short term memory. Immediate postoperative evaluation showed severe deficits in executive function (75 percent), attention (65 percent), left spatial neglect (60 percent), and behavioral disturbances including apathy, aprosodia and anosognosia. At 4 months group level z scores were largely stable except for a slight decline in categorical fluency, but individual level analysis showed decreased performance in at least one domain in 9 of 20 cases (45 percent), most often executive function. Spatial neglect mostly resolved by 4 months. 70 percent of previously working patients resumed work within 6 months, supporting the right frontal lobe as a highly eloquent area warranting awake mapping

Study Design: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data, single institution single surgeon
Tumor Type: Low grade glioma including astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, pleomorphic xanthoastrocytoma, dysembryoplastic neuroepithelial tumor, ganglioglioma, pilocytic astrocytoma, and oligoastrocytoma, all WHO grade I-II
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for tumor resection, with intraoperative awake mapping in 23 of 26 dominant hemisphere operations
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: IDH1-R132H, p53, and GFAP immunohistochemistry, and Ki-67/MIB proliferation index
Biomarker Biological Source: Formalin fixed paraffin embedded tumor tissue from resection specimen
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: IDH1 mutation, p53 and GFAP positivity examined as molecular correlates of cognitive outcome and resectability
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Determined once from routine surgical pathology, not a perioperative pre/post comparison
Neuropsychological Tests: Battery covering estimated premorbid intelligence, attention and working memory (digit span, spatial span), memory and learning (Rey complex figure, Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test), language (naming, semantic fluency), executive function (phonemic fluency, Stroop interference), and abstract thinking
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Test scores converted to z scores against normative data, domain score as the mean of tests within that domain, compared preoperatively to a follow up evaluation performed a mean of 6.06 months after surgery
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Comprehensive evaluation preoperatively and at follow up 3-28 months postoperatively (mean 6.06 months, subgroup analysis restricted to under 12 months mean 4.1 months)
Key Findings: Significant postoperative improvement was found in memory (p<.001) and executive function (p=.031). The subgroup with dominant side tumors, mostly awake mapped, showed significant improvement in both memory and executive function, while nondominant side tumors improved only in memory. P53 positivity was associated with better postoperative language function and a marginally greater extent of resection. GFAP positivity was associated with improved attention and working memory in nondominant side tumors. No correlation was found between cognitive outcome and IDH1 status, preoperative tumor volume, residual volume, or extent of resection

Tumor Type: Recurrent glioma in eloquent areas of the left hemisphere, low grade and high grade at recurrence (astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma)
Surgical Procedure: Awake repeat craniotomy for recurrent tumor resection with intraoperative mapping and real time neuropsychological testing
Sample Size (n): 40 patients, with a subgroup of 17 assessed across both first and second surgery
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 37 y SD11 (40 patient group), subgroup of 17 mean 35 y SD8.78
Sex Distribution: 68 percent male, 32 percent female (40 patient group)
Neuropsychological Tests: Verbal short term memory forward span, oral praxis, ideomotor limb apraxia, verbal comprehension (Token test), noun naming, verb naming, working memory span, and phonological fluency
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Number of patients scoring within the normal range per published cutoffs, and level of performance (accuracy), compared one week before versus one week after the second surgery and, in the subgroup, across all four timepoints spanning the first and second surgery
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Assessed one week before and one week after the second (recurrence) surgery and again 4 months later. The 17 patient subgroup was additionally assessed one week before and after the first surgery
Key Findings: No significant difference was found in the number of patients scoring within the normal range before versus after the second surgery for any test, nor in level of performance, except a very small but statistically significant decrease in oral praxis. In the subgroup followed from the first through the second surgery, only phonological fluency showed a significant decline across timepoints. Radiotherapy after the second surgery had no significant effect on cognitive scores. Greater extent of resection correlated negatively with verbal comprehension and phonological fluency. The authors concluded that repeated glioma surgery is feasible without major additional cognitive damage in the short term (4 month) follow up

Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumors identified by ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes, namely meningioma, glioma, brain metastases
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for brain tumor resection, identified by ICD-10-CM procedure codes
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Median 60 y in non-delirium group vs 67 y in delirium group
Sex Distribution: Delirium group 54.53% male vs 45.47% female. Non-delirium group 46.80% male vs 53.20% female
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Number of preoperative comorbidities (0, 1, 2, or 3 or more from a list of 32 conditions), used as a proxy for baseline frailty burden
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Identified from ICD-10-CM diagnostic codes (F05, F06, F0390, R410, R418) recorded during the index hospitalization before discharge
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Administrative coding based case ascertainment reflecting any delirium diagnosis documented before hospital discharge, not a prospective bedside instrument
Key Findings: Overall delirium incidence was 4.79 percent. Delirium patients were on average 7 years older, more often male, and more likely to have 3 or more comorbidities. Protective factors on multivariable analysis were self-pay status, elective admission, obesity, female sex, and private insurance. Delirium was associated with a 4 day longer median length of stay, about 41,700 dollars higher hospitalization cost, higher inpatient mortality (2.36 percent vs 1.28 percent), and higher rates of urinary tract infection, urinary retention, cerebral edema, acute renal failure, septicemia, pneumonia, and blood transfusion. Independent risk factors included psychoses, other neurological disorders, having 3 or more comorbidities, advanced age, alcohol abuse, peripheral vascular disorders, weight loss, hypertension, diabetes with chronic complications, fluid and electrolyte disorders, depression, paralysis, and smoking

Study Design: Single center, randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial (MAGNA study)
Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumor subgroup within a resective neurosurgery cohort (glioblastoma most common at 42.8 percent, also astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, meningioma, metastasis), analyzed alongside an epilepsy surgery subgroup
Surgical Procedure: Elective supratentorial resective craniotomy for brain tumor or epileptic focus. Intervention group received intravenous magnesium sulfate 4 g bolus over 20 minutes followed by 20 g over 24 hours starting at induction, control group received equal volume saline
Sample Size (n): 51 total (25 magnesium, 26 control). Brain tumor subgroup n=35 (18 magnesium, 17 control)
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 50 y SD14 for the full randomized cohort
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Neurovascular unit disruption. Biomarker release. Neurocognitive outcomes
Imaging Modality: 3T MRI including 3D FLAIR, diffusion tensor imaging, susceptibility weighted imaging, and pre and post gadolinium T1 MPRAGE, performed preoperatively, before hospital discharge, and at 6 months
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum S100B protein (primary outcome), neuron specific enolase, apolipoprotein E genotype, serum magnesium and calcium
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: S100B and neuron specific enolase used as surrogate markers of neuronal and glial injury and blood brain barrier disruption. Magnesium hypothesized to be neuroprotective via NMDA receptor antagonism and preservation of blood brain barrier integrity
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Baseline, 2 hours after surgery, then daily until postoperative day 10 for S100B. Similar schedule for neuron specific enolase
Neuropsychological Tests: Boston naming test, Auditory Verbal Learning Test, Logical Memory and Visual Reproduction I and II from the Wechsler Memory Scale, Digit Span forward and backward, Digit Symbol Coding, and Trail Making Test parts A and B
Radiological Outcome Definition: Gliosis or edema on FLAIR near the resection site, surgical cavity volume, and contrast enhancement around the cavity, each compared between baseline, before discharge, and 6 month MRI
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Raw scores on individual neuropsychological tests compared between treatment groups at each follow up timepoint, with subgroup analyses by tumor versus epilepsy surgery and by operated hemisphere
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Face to face 40 to 50 minute sessions administered by a blinded neuropsychologist preoperatively and at 1, 6, and 12 months after surgery
Key Findings: No significant between group difference was found in the primary outcome of serum S100B at 2 hours. At 6 months the magnesium group had a smaller surgical cavity volume (10.0 vs 26.9 cm3, p=.02), less gliosis or edema in the brain tumor subgroup (43.8 percent vs 85.7 percent, p=.02), and less contrast enhancement (33.3 percent vs 80 percent, p=.041), consistent with better preserved blood brain barrier integrity. The magnesium group also performed better on some declarative memory and attention or speed tests, particularly among brain tumor patients and depending on the operated hemisphere. No significant differences were found in Glasgow Outcome Scale or mortality at 6 or 12 months, and magnesium was well tolerated with transient hypermagnesemia resolving by postoperative day 2

Study Design: Retrospective analysis of a prospective cohort, single center
Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumors, benign and malignant, various supratentorial and infratentorial locations
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for brain tumor resection under general anesthesia, with postoperative ICU admission
Sample Size (n): 618 of 659 screened (41 excluded for coma-like state)
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Glasgow Coma Scale at ICU admission, modified Rankin Scale for long term functional outcome, Numeric Rating Scale for pain
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Emergence delirium defined as a Sedation-Agitation Scale (SAS) score of 5 to 7, hypoactive (RASS -3 to -1) or hyperactive (RASS 1 to 4), assessed with the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU. Separate postoperative delirium (POD) assessed on postoperative day 1 and day 3
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale followed by CAM-ICU assessed within 2 hours of ICU admission for emergence delirium. CAM-ICU repeated on postoperative day 1 and day 3 for POD
Key Findings: Emergence delirium occurred in 21.2 percent of patients (131 of 618), predominantly hypoactive (83.2 percent). Independent risk factors were age, education level, use of anticholinergic drugs and mannitol, lower postoperative GCS score and PaO2, postoperative pain, malignant tumor, and frontal approach craniotomy. Emergence delirium was associated with a markedly higher rate of subsequent postoperative delirium (58.8 percent vs 4.7 percent), longer hospital stay (13 vs 10 days), and higher hospitalization cost, though it was not associated with worse modified Rankin Scale functional outcome

Study Design: Prospective, randomized, double blind, controlled trial
Tumor Type: Supratentorial brain tumors including meningioma, glioblastoma, astrocytoma, and metastases
Surgical Procedure: Elective supratentorial craniotomy for tumor resection, comparing 3 mL/kg (low dose) versus 5 mL/kg (high dose) of 3 percent hypertonic saline given at skin incision for intraoperative brain relaxation
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 50 y SD16 (low dose) vs 49 y SD16 (high dose)
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum osmolality, sodium, chloride, potassium, glucose, lactate, hematocrit, hemoglobin, platelet count, and fibrinogen
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Before hypertonic saline infusion and at 30, 120, and 360 minutes after infusion
Hemodynamic Measurements: Mean arterial pressure, central venous pressure, cardiac index, stroke volume index, systemic vascular resistance index, and stroke volume variation via arterial line and pulse contour analysis, recorded before infusion and at 30, 120, and 360 minutes
Radiological Outcome Definition: Presence and magnitude of preoperative midline shift greater than 1 mm on MRI used to stratify brain relaxation response, rather than a postoperative imaging endpoint
Key Findings: Median brain relaxation score was identical between the low dose and high dose groups (2.0 for both, p=.535), and among patients with midline shift only about half achieved adequate relaxation regardless of dose. Both doses produced comparable sustained rises in serum osmolality, sodium, and chloride for 6 hours and comparable falls in hematocrit, platelet count, and fibrinogen consistent with plasma volume expansion. The low dose group required more intraoperative fluid input and had greater urine output than the high dose group. Hemodynamic parameters were otherwise similar between groups, and postoperative complications, PCU stay, hospital stay, and 30 day mortality did not differ

Study Design: Study protocol for a prospective, randomized, double blind, controlled trial (TINSI trial). No outcome results reported at time of this publication
Tumor Type: Supratentorial glioma
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for supratentorial glioma resection, comparing propofol based total intravenous anesthesia versus sevoflurane based inhalational anesthesia
Sample Size (n): Planned 45 patients per group (90 total). Enrollment ongoing at time of publication
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Perioperative brain injury. Neuroinflammation. Neurocognitive outcomes
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Planned measurement of neuron specific enolase and interleukin-6, pre- and post-anesthesia
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Neuron specific enolase proposed as a marker of neuronal inflammation and interleukin-6 as a marker of systemic inflammation, both hypothesized to link intraoperative neuroinflammation to postoperative neurocognitive dysfunction
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Planned baseline sample before anesthesia induction and a second sample at the end of surgery
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Karnofsky Performance Status (preoperative score below 70 is an exclusion criterion) and ASA physical status
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Planned assessment using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU twice daily during ICU stay, followed by ward-based CAM assessment for up to 7 postoperative days
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Planned twice daily CAM-ICU during ICU stay, then daily ward CAM up to postoperative day 7
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Planned use of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment for postoperative cognitive dysfunction between postoperative day 5 and 7 or at discharge, the Brief Screen for Cognitive Impairment by telephone at 4 weeks after discharge, and the Glasgow Outcome Scale at discharge and 3 months
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Planned baseline testing before anesthesia, in-hospital testing around postoperative day 5-7 or discharge, and telephonic follow up 4 weeks after discharge
Key Findings: This is a trial protocol without empirical outcome data at the time of this publication. The study hypothesizes that propofol based TIVA will show a lower neuronal and systemic inflammatory profile than sevoflurane based inhalational anesthesia and correspondingly less postoperative neurocognitive dysfunction. The first patient was recruited in September 2023 with completion anticipated by March 2025, and results were not yet available

Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumors, glioma and non-glioma, supratentorial and infratentorial
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for brain tumor resection with postoperative ICU admission
Imaging Modality: Postoperative CT scan obtained within 6 hours of surgery, retrospectively reviewed in blinded fashion by two neuroradiologists for bi-frontal subdural pneumocephalus and the Mount Fuji sign
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Glasgow Coma Scale at ICU admission and modified Rankin Scale for long term neurological outcome
Radiological Outcome Definition: Bi-frontal pneumocephalus defined as bilateral subdural hypoattenuation in the frontal region present on at least four axial slices with frontal lobe displacement from the dura of more than 1 cm in at least one slice. The Mount Fuji sign identified as a distinct subtype with collapsed frontal lobes and widened interhemispheric space
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Agitation defined as a Sedation-Agitation Scale score of 5 to 7, assessed hourly until the patient could follow commands and then every 4 hours for up to 24 hours or until ICU discharge
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Sedation-Agitation Scale assessed by trained ICU staff during the first 24 postoperative hours
Key Findings: Agitation occurred in 13.0 percent of patients. Independent multivariable risk factors were bi-frontal pneumocephalus (odds ratio 4.4) and delayed extubation, whether without mechanical ventilation (odds ratio 3.6) or with mechanical ventilation (odds ratio 5.2). Bi-frontal pneumocephalus was more frequent after frontal approach surgery (35.8 percent vs 13.7 percent) and supratentorial tumor surgery (27.8 percent vs 16.8 percent). After adjustment for confounders, postoperative agitation was independently associated with poor grade modified Rankin Scale outcome (odds ratio 5.4) but not with longer hospital stay

Study Design: Single center, randomized, controlled trial with patient and outcome assessor blinding
Tumor Type: Supratentorial tumors (glioma, meningioma, metastatic, other) with preoperative midline shift under 5 mm
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for supratentorial tumor resection, comparing desflurane anesthesia versus propofol based total intravenous anesthesia
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Brain tumor microenvironment. Neurovascular unit disruption. Neurocognitive outcomes
Hemodynamic Measurements: Mean arterial pressure, bispectral index, and PaCO2 monitored continuously, along with vasopressor and vasodilator requirements, compared between groups
Radiological Outcome Definition: Preoperative peritumoral edema graded on MRI T2 sequence using the Steinhoff classification (none, mild, moderate, severe), used as a predictor of brain relaxation rather than a postoperative outcome
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Short Orientation Memory Concentration Test score, ranging 0 to 28, as a measure of early postoperative cognitive recovery
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Administered by the attending anesthesiologist at 15 and 30 minutes after tracheal extubation
Key Findings: The proportion of satisfactory brain relaxation was similar between desflurane (69 percent) and TIVA (73 percent) groups. Peritumoral edema grade and occipital tumor location, not anesthesia type, were independent predictors of unsatisfactory brain relaxation. Desflurane produced significantly faster emergence (10 vs 13 minutes) and extubation (13 vs 17 minutes) and better cognitive recovery scores at 15 minutes after extubation (16 vs 0, p=.003), but was associated with more postoperative nausea and vomiting (29 percent vs 11 percent) and tachycardia (40 percent vs 16 percent) during recovery

Study Design: Randomized, double blind, placebo controlled study
Tumor Type: Cerebral tumors scheduled for elective resection with baseline intracranial pressure 20 mmHg or less
