Surgical Procedure: Elective cerebral tumor resection under propofol based total intravenous anesthesia. Clonidine 3 microgram per kilogram or placebo given 10 minutes before induction
Hemodynamic Measurements: Continuous invasive mean arterial pressure and lumbar cerebrospinal fluid pressure as an ICP surrogate, recorded every minute during preinduction, induction, intubation, Mayfield head-holder application, and incision. Cerebral perfusion pressure calculated as MAP minus ICP
Key Findings: Clonidine had no effect on ICP or heart rate at any timepoint. Clonidine significantly lowered mean arterial pressure and cerebral perfusion pressure from the preinduction period onward, and this lower baseline persisted through induction, intubation, Mayfield application, and incision, without preventing the relative rise in MAP, ICP, or CPP evoked by each noxious stimulus. Propofol requirements for induction and intubation were significantly lower with clonidine (2.08 vs 3.3 mg per kilogram, p less than .05), though total case propofol and fentanyl requirements were unchanged. 8 of 12 clonidine treated patients had at least one episode of cerebral perfusion pressure below 60 mmHg versus 2 of 12 placebo patients, while 8 placebo patients versus 1 clonidine patient had cerebral perfusion pressure above 110 mmHg. The authors concluded clonidine acts as a partial sympatholytic that resets baseline MAP and CPP downward without altering ICP or blunting stimulus evoked increases

Country: USA (multi-institution, namely Duke, University of Iowa, Columbia)
Study Design: Prospective, multi-institution, randomized, double blind trial
Tumor Type: Supratentorial space occupying lesions including meningioma, glioma, and metastasis
Surgical Procedure: Elective supratentorial craniotomy, comparing remifentanil versus fentanyl as the primary opioid with nitrous oxide based anesthesia and isoflurane rescue as needed
Sample Size (n): 63 (32 fentanyl, 31 remifentanil). ICP subset n=16 fentanyl and 17 remifentanil
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 49 y SD13 (fentanyl) vs 51 y SD13 (remifentanil)
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Perioperative brain injury. Neurovascular unit disruption
Hemodynamic Measurements: Systolic blood pressure and heart rate recorded continuously through induction, intubation, maintenance, emergence, and recovery. Intracranial pressure measured epidurally at the first burr hole in a subset of patients without prior craniotomy
Radiological Outcome Definition: Preoperative CT or MRI graded for maximum tumor diameter, midline shift, and mass effect (none, mild, moderate, severe) as baseline covariates rather than a postoperative outcome measure
Neurological Deficit Definition: Standardized neurologic examination covering mental status, cranial nerves, motor, sensory, cerebellar function, and gait, categorized as normal or abnormal
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Senior neurosurgery resident examination performed before operation and on postoperative days 1 and 7
Key Findings: Systolic blood pressure after intubation was higher with fentanyl (127 vs 113 mmHg, p=.004). Intraoperative ICP (14 vs 13 mmHg), cerebral perfusion pressure (76 vs 78 mmHg), and brain relaxation scores were similar between groups. More fentanyl patients required naloxone for delayed emergence (seven vs zero). Postoperative systolic blood pressure was higher and analgesics were needed earlier in the remifentanil group. Nausea and vomiting rates were similar. Neurologic examination changes from screening to postoperative day 1 and day 7 were broadly similar between groups, with most new deficits involving motor and cranial nerve function in both arms. The authors concluded remifentanil is a reasonable alternative to fentanyl for elective supratentorial craniotomy

Journal: Journal of Neuroanaesthesiology and Critical Care
Study Design: Prospective, randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial
Tumor Type: Supratentorial meningioma
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for tumor removal, with intravenous magnesium sulfate 40 mg per kilogram loading over 30 minutes starting at skin incision followed by 10 mg per kilogram per hour infusion until dura closure, versus saline placebo
Sex Distribution: 34F/4M in each group (89.5 percent female overall)
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Baseline and 4 hours after infusion start for magnesium level. Hematocrit every 2 to 3 hours intraoperatively
Cognitive Outcome Definition: MoCA score, range 0 to 30, with 26 or higher considered normal
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Day before surgery and postoperative day 3 to 7
Key Findings: Intraoperative blood loss did not differ significantly between magnesium (500 mL) and control (510 mL) groups. Anesthetic requirement, intraoperative mean arterial pressure, hypotensive episodes, vasopressor use, and transfusion rates were similar between groups. Postoperative MoCA scores did not differ significantly between groups, though sample size was underpowered for this outcome. Serum magnesium levels rose but did not reach toxic levels and no adverse events attributable to magnesium were observed

Country: India (multi-center, namely Bengaluru, Vellore, Puducherry, Trivandrum, Hyderabad)
Study Design: Study protocol for a prospective, multi-center, randomized controlled trial (NOPAIN trial). No outcome results reported at time of this publication
Tumor Type: Supratentorial brain tumors
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy, comparing fentanyl 1 microgram per kilogram per hour versus dexmedetomidine 0.5 microgram per kilogram per hour as the primary intraoperative systemic analgesic
Sample Size (n): Planned 500 patients (250 per group), 100 enrolled per center across 5 centers
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: ASA physical status and Glasgow Coma Scale (inclusion requires GCS 15)
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Planned assessment of emergence delirium and quality of recovery using the Riker Sedation Agitation Scale at 15 and 60 minutes in the post-anesthesia care unit, as a secondary outcome
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Planned Riker Sedation Agitation Scale assessment at 15 and 60 minutes postoperatively in the recovery unit
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Not a primary cognitive outcome measure. Planned secondary outcomes include quality of recovery, sleep quality by Likert scale, and persistent pain and quality of life at 3 and 6 months
Key Findings: This is a trial protocol without empirical outcome data at the time of this publication. The hypothesis is that dexmedetomidine will be non-inferior or superior to fentanyl for intraoperative rescue opioid requirement and postoperative pain, the co-primary outcomes, with secondary outcomes covering adverse events, quality of recovery including emergence delirium, sleep quality, and long term persistent pain and quality of life. The first patient was recruited in October 2022 with recruitment completion planned before March 2024, and results were not yet available

Study Design: Randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial, two centers
Tumor Type: Frontotemporal brain tumors, predominantly glioma, also meningioma and other histologies
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for intracerebral tumor resection, with intravenous dexmedetomidine 0.6 microgram per kilogram loading dose followed by 0.4 microgram per kilogram per hour infusion until dural closure, versus saline placebo
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Mini-Mental State Examination required above 20 for inclusion, WHO tumor grade, and Charlson Comorbidity Index
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Assessed twice daily for the first 5 postoperative days using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU or the 3 minute Diagnostic interview CAM for ward patients, combined with the Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale, with motoric subtypes classified as hyperactive, hypoactive, or mixed
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Twice daily, morning and evening, assessments for the first 5 postoperative days by trained assessors blinded to treatment
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Mini-Mental State Examination score on postoperative day 5 as a secondary cognitive outcome
Key Findings: Incidence of delirium during the first 5 postoperative days was 22 percent with dexmedetomidine versus 46 percent with placebo (risk ratio 0.51, p less than .001), consistent across hyperactive, hypoactive, and mixed subtypes and across all predefined subgroups. Dexmedetomidine reduced pain with movement, improved sleep quality and quality of recovery, and produced higher postoperative day 5 Mini-Mental State Examination scores, without increasing intraoperative hypotension or bradycardia. Gliomas were roughly twice as likely to develop delirium as other tumor types regardless of treatment assignment

Tumor Type: Mixed craniocerebral (brain) tumors undergoing elective craniotomy
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for brain tumor resection under general anesthesia, with electroacupuncture preconditioning at Fengfu (Du16) and Fengchi (GB20) acupoints for 30 minutes, 2 hours before induction, versus no pretreatment control
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum S100 calcium binding protein beta (S100 beta) and neuron specific enolase (NSE)
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: S100 beta and NSE are markers of astrocyte and neuronal injury respectively, released into blood after blood brain barrier disruption from surgical brain injury
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Before induction, before skin incision, after tumor removal, at end of operation, and 24 hours after operation
Key Findings: Serum S100 beta and NSE did not change before skin incision in either group. NSE rose significantly after tumor removal in both groups. At the end of the operation and 24 hours postoperatively, both S100 beta and NSE were significantly lower in the electroacupuncture group than in the control group (S100 beta 1.16 vs 1.47 microgram per liter at end of surgery, NSE 24.7 vs 31.4 microgram per liter at end of surgery, both p less than .05). Hemodynamic and respiratory parameters did not differ between groups. The authors concluded electroacupuncture preconditioning may have a protective effect against surgically induced brain injury

Study Design: Prospective, randomized, double blind, placebo controlled, three arm comparative study
Tumor Type: Supratentorial brain tumors, excluding tumors larger than 30 mm in any dimension
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for supratentorial tumor excision, comparing intravenous lignocaine (1.5 mg per kilogram bolus then 2 mg per kilogram per hour infusion), normal saline placebo, or magnesium sulfate (50 mg per kilogram bolus then 25 mg per kilogram per hour infusion), all given intraoperatively
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: S100B is a marker of glial and neuronal injury, used here to compare relative neuroprotective effect of the study drugs
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Baseline before drug administration, end of surgery, and 24 hours postoperatively
Key Findings: Mean postoperative visual analog scale pain scores over 24 hours were significantly lower with lignocaine (15.3) and magnesium (17.9) compared to saline (24.8, p less than .01). 24 hour postoperative fentanyl consumption via patient controlled analgesia was significantly lower with lignocaine (204.4 microgram) and magnesium (194 microgram) than saline (383 microgram, p=.01). Intraoperative fentanyl use, hemodynamics, and recovery times were comparable across groups with no adverse effects. Serum S100B did not differ between lignocaine and saline groups, but was significantly lower at 24 hours postoperatively in the magnesium group compared to the other two groups, suggesting a possible neuroprotective effect of magnesium

Tumor Type: Meningioma, mostly larger than 3 cm in diameter and selected for surgical treatment
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for meningioma resection
Neuropsychological Tests: CNS Vital Signs computerized battery covering verbal and visual memory, psychomotor speed, reaction time, complex attention, cognitive flexibility, processing speed, and executive functioning. Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale also administered
Radiological Outcome Definition: Tumor location categorized by hemisphere (left, right, bilateral), supratentorial versus infratentorial, and skull base versus convexity versus falx, used to test association with cognitive outcome rather than as a standalone postoperative outcome
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Age corrected standard scores (mean 100, SD 15) per domain compared against American normative data. Individual patients classified as scoring low or very low (1.5 to 2 SD below average) per domain. Change in severity category from pre to postoperative assessment tracked per patient
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: One day before surgery and 3 months after surgery
Key Findings: Meningioma patients scored significantly lower than normative controls in all 7 cognitive domains both before and after surgery. Preoperatively 69 percent of patients (47 of 68) scored low or very low in at least one domain, decreasing to 44 percent (27 of 62) postoperatively. Significant improvement was found in 5 of 7 domains, memory, complex attention, cognitive flexibility, processing speed, and executive functioning, 3 months after surgery, with no significant improvement in psychomotor speed or reaction time. No significant associations were found between tumor location and either baseline cognitive status or degree of postoperative improvement, except that infratentorial tumors showed better postoperative complex attention than supratentorial tumors. Anxiety and depression symptom levels both decreased significantly after surgery

Study Design: Prospective, randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial
Tumor Type: Supratentorial brain tumors, including glioblastoma or anaplastic astrocytoma, low grade glioma, metastasis, and meningioma
Surgical Procedure: Elective supratentorial craniotomy, with magnesium sulfate 5 g infused over 6 hours given 2 days before surgery, repeated the day before and during surgery, versus placebo saline
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum S100B protein and neuron specific enolase (NSE)
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: S100B and NSE are established biomarkers of glial and neuronal injury respectively, with serum elevation reflecting the intensity of brain injury
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: 2 days before surgery before magnesium administration, immediately after surgery, and on postoperative day 2
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Not assessed with a formal neuropsychological battery. Functional outcome assessed via the Barthel index of activities of daily living rather than cognitive domain testing
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Barthel index evaluated before surgery and at 3 and 6 months after surgery
Key Findings: Serum S100B differed significantly between groups over time, with a smaller postoperative rise in the magnesium group than in placebo. NSE increased over time in all patients but did not differ significantly between groups at any timepoint. Barthel index scores decreased over time in all patients with no significant difference between groups. The magnesium group had significantly lower intraoperative mean arterial pressure, heart rate, blood loss, and propofol requirement. NSE and S100B were positively correlated, and postoperative NSE, but not S100B, correlated negatively with Barthel index. The authors concluded magnesium sulfate reduces S100B elevation, a marker of brain injury, though this was not reflected in a significant difference in functional outcome at this sample size

Study Design: Prospective randomized controlled study, three parallel arms
Tumor Type: Supratentorial brain tumors (47 right sided, 13 left sided)
Surgical Procedure: Elective resection of supratentorial brain tumor, comparing three intraoperative maintenance infusates during the first 2 hours of surgery, crystalloid (normal saline), colloid (Hemaccel), or blood
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Range 20-60 y. Mean 36.6 y crystalloid, 42.3 y colloid, 41.15 y blood
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Paired arterial and jugular bulb blood gases, hemoglobin, hematocrit, blood glucose, and jugular venous lactate
Biomarker Biological Source: Paired arterial and jugular bulb blood samples
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Jugular venous oxygen saturation and derived cerebral metabolic rate for oxygen, cerebral oxygen extraction ratio, and cerebral blood flow equivalent used as indices of cerebral oxygen delivery, consumption, and flow metabolism coupling
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Immediately after induction, then every 30 minutes for 2 hours, and after dural closure
Hemodynamic Measurements: Heart rate, non-invasive mean arterial pressure, and central venous pressure recorded every 30 minutes throughout surgery
Key Findings: Colloid maintenance was associated with significantly higher jugular venous oxygen saturation throughout surgery compared with crystalloid, and a significantly higher cerebral blood flow equivalent compared with both crystalloid and blood, consistent with better preserved flow metabolism coupling. The blood group showed a significant rise in cerebral metabolic rate for oxygen and a fall in cerebral blood flow equivalent from baseline, along with higher blood lactate and glucose at the second hour compared with colloid. Hemoglobin and hematocrit fell in the crystalloid and colloid groups but rose in the blood group. The authors concluded colloid was the most effective infusate for maintaining cerebral oxygen delivery and flow metabolism coupling during brain tumor resection

Study Design: Randomized, double blind, placebo controlled trial
Tumor Type: Supratentorial tumors (glioma, meningioma, other)
Surgical Procedure: Elective supratentorial craniotomy, with intravenous lidocaine bolus 1.5 mg per kilogram followed by 2 mg per kilogram per hour infusion until end of surgery, versus equal volume saline
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Cerebral oxygen extraction ratio, glucose extraction ratio, and arteriovenous lactate difference derived from paired arterial and jugular venous bulb blood sampling
Biomarker Biological Source: Paired arterial and internal jugular venous bulb blood samples
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Cerebral oxygen extraction ratio and arteriovenous lactate difference used as indices of cerebral oxygen utilization and anaerobic metabolism, to test whether lidocaine reduces cerebral metabolic demand
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Before drug administration, then 1, 2, 3 hours after start of infusion and at end of surgery
Neuropsychological Tests: Mini-Mental State Examination, Information-Memory-Concentration test, Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression, Hamilton Rating Scale for Anxiety
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Postoperative neuropsychological cognitive decline defined as a decline of at least the preoperative standard deviation on two or more of the four tests, assessed serially up to 6 months
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Preoperative baseline and postoperative 24 hours, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months, by blinded psychometricians
Key Findings: Incidence of neuropsychological cognitive decline at 6 months did not differ significantly between lidocaine and saline groups, either on the preplanned analysis or on post hoc analyses restricted to the two pure cognitive tests. Only about 10 percent of patients in either group showed cognitive dysfunction by 6 months. Lidocaine significantly reduced cerebral oxygen extraction ratio at end of surgery and reduced arteriovenous lactate difference at 1, 2, and 3 hours and end of surgery compared with saline, suggesting reduced cerebral oxygen utilization and anaerobic metabolism, but this metabolic effect did not translate into a measurable cognitive benefit

Study Design: Prospective cohort study with factor analysis and voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping
Tumor Type: Glioma, left hemisphere (n=33) and right hemisphere (n=21), WHO grade II to IV
Surgical Procedure: Intraoperative MRI guided glioma resection, including awake surgery in a subset of patients
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 41.5 y (left glioma) vs 36.7 y (right glioma)
Imaging Modality: Preoperative 1.5T MRI for lesion delineation, with postoperative MRI at 6 months used to correct resected region boundaries for voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping
Neuropsychological Tests: Seven tasks across five cognitive domains, visual-verbal learning, word fluency, digit span forward and backward, letter-digit substitution, concept shifting, and Stroop color-word task, plus MMSE-J, Rey-Osterrieth complex figure, and line bisection for baseline screening
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Postoperative z scores on each task relative to preoperative mean and standard deviation, with factor analysis used to extract common cognitive components across tasks and voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping used to identify associated brain regions
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Preoperative (mean 9.7 days before surgery) and 6 months postoperatively
Key Findings: In the left glioma group, one cognitive component reflecting digit span and concept shifting performance mapped to the posterior superior and middle temporal gyri and supramarginal gyrus, while a second component reflecting verbal learning and word fluency mapped to medial temporal and posterior parietal regions. In the right glioma group, a component reflecting Stroop task performance mapped to the anterior medial frontal cortex, while an inhibitory component mapped to the right inferior frontal cortex. MMSE-J, Rey-Osterrieth figure copy, and line bisection scores remained within normal range at both timepoints in both groups, indicating that basic cognitive screening did not capture the more specific primary cognitive deficits identified by the detailed task battery and lesion mapping

Study Design: Prospective cohort study combining functional MRI and neuropsychological assessment
Tumor Type: Meningioma (WHO grade I n=21, grade II n=2), supratentorial
Surgical Procedure: Elective meningioma resection
Imaging Modality: 3T functional MRI using a verbal 2-back working memory task, region of interest analysis of central executive network and default mode network, acquired 1 to 5 days before and 3 months after surgery
Neuropsychological Tests: Central Nervous System Vital Signs battery, specifically symbol digit coding, Stroop III, and a shifting attention task, all involving working memory
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Socio-demographically adjusted z scores on neuropsychological tests compared with normative data, in-scanner task accuracy, and blood oxygen level dependent signal change within central executive and default mode network regions of interest during the 2-back versus 0-back task conditions
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: 1 to 5 days before surgery and 3 months after surgery, on the same days as fMRI scanning
Key Findings: Meningioma patients performed significantly worse than normative data on all three neuropsychological tests both before and after surgery, with no significant improvement 3 months postoperatively. In-scanner task performance did not change between timepoints. Brain activity within the central executive network and default mode network during the working memory task did not differ significantly between preoperative and postoperative scans, either at the network level or for any individual region of interest. The authors concluded that the lack of cognitive improvement after meningioma surgery is not explained by compensatory brain activity changes, and that preoperative cognitive deficits tend to persist in the first few months after resection

Tumor Type: Brain metastases
Surgical Procedure: Brain metastasis resection (craniotomy)
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Risk Analysis Index (categorized as robust 0-20, normal 21-30, frail 31-40, severely frail 41 or more) and 5-factor modified frailty index, both calculated from preoperative demographic and comorbidity data
Key Findings: Overall 30-day mortality was 4.2 percent and increased progressively with Risk Analysis Index category, from 1.3 percent in robust patients to 12.6 percent in severely frail patients. The Risk Analysis Index showed superior discrimination for predicting 30-day mortality compared with the modified frailty index and chronological age (C-statistic 0.65, p less than .001 by DeLong test). Severely frail patients had significantly higher rates of major complications, high grade Clavien-Dindo complications, extended length of stay, and non-home discharge. In logistic regression, frail and severely frail categories carried 2.7 and 9.9 times higher odds of 30-day mortality respectively compared with robust patients. The authors developed a publicly available online calculator for estimating 30-day mortality risk using this frailty index in brain metastasis resection candidates
Evidence stream: Systemic frailty indices and perioperative risk

Tumor Type: Suspected lower-grade glioma (WHO II-III) in the inferior primary motor cortex face area, with two cases found to be glioblastoma (WHO IV) on final pathology
Surgical Procedure: Awake craniotomy resection in the lower primary motor cortex face area, using an asleep-awake-asleep technique with intraoperative motor evoked potential and speech mapping
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: House-Brackmann Facial Nerve Grading Scale, Facial Clinimetric Evaluation questionnaire, Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale, Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function-Adult version, and Mental Fatigue Scale
Neuropsychological Tests: Verbal fluency and color word interference task from the Delis-Kaplan Executive Function System, Brief Visual Memory Test-Revised, and Digit Span from WAIS-IV
Neurological Deficit Definition: Facial motor dysfunction graded on the House-Brackmann scale from 1 to 6, with 1 representing full recovery, affecting mouth, tongue, and throat movement
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: House-Brackmann grading and Facial Clinimetric Evaluation questionnaire administered retrospectively at a mean of 1.2 years after surgery
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Change in raw and standardized scores on verbal fluency, color word interference, visual memory, and digit span tasks from preoperative to postoperative assessment
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Preoperative and postoperative, mean 5.9 months after surgery, range 2.2-12.9 months
Key Findings: Six of seven patients developed mild facial motor dysfunction postoperatively, mainly affecting the mouth, tongue, and throat, classified as mild on the House-Brackmann scale. There was a significant postoperative decline in maximal verbal processing speed on the color naming, reading, and switching conditions of the color word interference task, but no significant change in verbal fluency, long-term memory, or working memory. Quality of life measured by EORTC QLQ-C30 and BN-20 did not change significantly except for a decline in social function that was attributable to unrelated COVID-19 self-quarantine in two patients rather than a direct surgical effect. Self-reported anxiety, depression, and everyday executive function did not change significantly, though there was a non-significant trend toward increased postoperative anxiety. The authors concluded that awake resection of the lower face motor cortex can be performed safely with mild and generally tolerable postoperative deficits

Journal: arXiv preprint (not yet peer reviewed at time of extraction)
Country: USA (data originally collected at Ghent University Hospital, Belgium)
Study Design: Retrospective analysis of a publicly available neuroimaging dataset using high-order energy landscape modeling and machine learning
Tumor Type: Supratentorial glioma (WHO grade II-III, n=7) and meningioma (WHO grade I-II, n=13)
Surgical Procedure: Surgical resection of glioma or meningioma
Imaging Modality: Preoperative resting-state functional MRI (3T), used to derive high-order energy landscape features via k-means functional clustering and maximum entropy modeling, compared against low-order features from canonical resting-state networks including default mode, salience, sensorimotor, and limbic networks
Neuropsychological Tests: Spatial Span test for working memory, administered before and 6 months after surgery, used to classify patients into low (score 2-5) versus high (score 6-9) postoperative working memory performance groups
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Binary classification of postoperative working memory performance, low versus high, based on Spatial Span score at 6 months after surgery
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Preoperative and 6 months postoperative Spatial Span testing
Key Findings: Patients with low postoperative working memory performance showed fewer but more extreme energy transitions in the high-order energy landscape derived from presurgical resting-state fMRI, while patients with high performance showed more frequent but less extreme transitions. High-order energy features showed significant group differences in extreme energy values and transition frequency and magnitude, while low-order canonical network features generally did not reach significance. A random forest model using high-order energy features predicted postoperative working memory group with a mean accuracy of 90 percent, F1 score of 87.5 percent, and AUC of 0.95, significantly outperforming models based on low-order network features. The authors propose that presurgical high-order neural dynamics could serve as a predictive biomarker for postoperative working memory decline, though this is an early-stage computational finding from a preprint that has not completed peer review and requires prospective validation

Tumor Type: Meningioma (craniocerebral tumor)
Surgical Procedure: Meningioma resection, comparing ciprofol (0.5 mg per kilogram induction, 1.5 to 2 mg per kilogram per hour maintenance) versus propofol (1.5 to 2 mg per kilogram induction, 5 to 8 mg per kilogram per hour maintenance)
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum neuron specific enolase and S100 beta protein
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Neuron specific enolase and S100 beta used as markers of neuronal and glial injury respectively, to compare the relative neuroprotective effect of the two anesthetic agents
Hemodynamic Measurements: Heart rate and systolic and diastolic arterial blood pressure recorded before anesthesia, immediately before intubation, 3 minutes after intubation, immediately after complete tumor resection, and at end of surgery
Key Findings: Heart rate and arterial blood pressure were significantly higher in the ciprofol group immediately before and 3 minutes after intubation compared with propofol, but did not differ at other timepoints, and the incidence of induction related hypotension was markedly lower with ciprofol (59 percent vs 95 percent, p less than .001). Eye opening time was slightly longer with ciprofol (23.1 vs 20.9 minutes, p=.014). Postoperative serum S100 beta and neuron specific enolase at 24 hours were significantly higher in the ciprofol group than the propofol group, indicating ciprofol was not superior to propofol for cerebral protection despite its more stable hemodynamic profile during induction

Study Design: Prospective cohort study (two combined recruitment cohorts)
Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumors (meningioma, high-grade glioma, low-grade glioma, pituitary adenoma, vestibular schwannoma, metastatic tumor)
Surgical Procedure: Elective cranial surgery, craniotomy or stereotactic biopsy
Age (mean/median, range or SD): POD group 66.91 y (SD9.61) vs no-POD group 56.81 y (SD15.04)
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Hemoglobin, red blood cell count, platelet count, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, and NT-proBNP
Biomarker Biological Source: Peripheral venous blood drawn on first day of admission
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: Low hemoglobin and elevated NT-proBNP tested as candidate predictors of delirium, reflecting anemia-related reduced cerebral oxygen delivery and cardiovascular stress respectively
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Barthel Index (cohort 1), Karnofsky Performance Index and Modified Rankin Scale (cohort 2) for preoperative functional status, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale
Biomarker Outcome Definition: Predefined normal reference ranges used to dichotomize biomarkers, namely hemoglobin 119-146 g/L, red blood cell count 3.9-5.1x10^12/L, platelet count 166-308x10^9/L, NT-proBNP under 157 ng/L (cohort 1) or under 125 ng/L (cohort 2), high-sensitivity CRP 3.0 mg/L or less, interleukin-6 0-7 pg/mL (cohort 1) or 0-5.9 pg/mL (cohort 2). Values outside these ranges categorized as low or high for analysis
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Delirium diagnosed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU, requiring acute onset or fluctuating mental status plus inattention, along with either disorganized thinking or altered level of consciousness
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: CAM-ICU performed daily for 2 consecutive days (cohort 1) or 7 consecutive days (cohort 2) after surgery by trained investigators on the hospital ward
Key Findings: Postoperative delirium occurred in 4.2 percent of patients. Independent predictors on multivariate analysis were age 65 years or older, less than secondary education, poor preoperative functional status, and low hemoglobin concentration, while brain tumor laterality, location, extent of resection, and histological diagnosis were not associated with delirium risk. Patients with delirium had significantly worse Glasgow Outcome Scale scores at hospital discharge, and delirium independently predicted unfavorable discharge outcome with an odds ratio of 5.3

Tumor Type: WHO grade I meningioma, postoperative, without adjuvant treatment
Surgical Procedure: Tumor resection, assessed postoperatively at a mean of 1.7 years after surgery
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Mean 51.4 y (SD10.9) patients vs 51.6 y (SD11.0) controls
Imaging Modality: Postoperative magnetoencephalography (151-channel), source-space functional connectivity (phase lag index) within the default mode network and bilateral frontoparietal networks, and minimum spanning tree graph-theoretical network topology analysis
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Barthel Index for functional and performance status, reported for the patient group (mean 19.8, SD0.8)
Neuropsychological Tests: Standardized battery covering executive functioning, working memory, verbal memory, attention, information processing speed, and psychomotor speed, converted to z scores against matched healthy controls
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Cognitive dysfunction defined as a z score at least 1.5 SD below the healthy control mean in a given domain, with working memory as the primary outcome
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Single postoperative assessment, mean 1.7 years (range 0.4 to 4.6 years) after tumor resection
Key Findings: Meningioma patients had significantly lower working memory capacity than healthy controls. Within the patient group, lower working memory performance correlated with lower default mode network connectivity in the theta band and with lower maximum minimum-spanning-tree degree in the theta band, while no significant associations emerged for other cognitive domains, other resting-state networks, or other frequency bands, pointing to a specific link between disrupted theta-band network organization and working memory deficits after meningioma surgery

Tumor Type: Supratentorial brain tumor (glioma and meningioma)
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy for supratentorial tumor resection, comparing goal-directed fluid therapy using a low stroke volume variation threshold of 10 percent versus a high threshold of 18 percent to trigger colloid boluses
Age (mean/median, range or SD): Median 55 y (low SVV) vs 58 y (high SVV)
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Perioperative brain injury. Neurovascular unit disruption. Biomarker release
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum S100b, neuron specific enolase, glial fibrillary acidic protein, and brain natriuretic peptide
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: S100b, NSE, and GFAP used as markers of neuronal and glial injury, brain natriuretic peptide used as an indicator of intravascular volume status
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Baseline before surgery, end of surgery, postoperative day 1, and postoperative day 2 (BNP and lactate at baseline and end of surgery only)
Hemodynamic Measurements: Stroke volume variation, cardiac index, mean arterial pressure, heart rate, and systolic blood pressure monitored continuously via arterial line and pulse-contour analysis throughout surgery
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Barthel Index for activities of daily living, assessed at hospital admission and discharge
Neurological Deficit Definition: New postoperative neurological event classified per International Statistical Classification of Diseases criteria
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Clinical assessment during hospitalization, and Barthel Index at admission and discharge
Key Findings: The low stroke volume variation group received more colloid, had a higher intraoperative cardiac index, shorter ICU stay, and fewer new postoperative neurological events (17.5 percent vs 40 percent) than the high threshold group. The low SVV group also had attenuated postoperative rises in serum NSE and GFAP and a higher Barthel Index at discharge, while S100b did not differ between groups. Intraoperative serum lactate rose significantly in the high SVV group but not the low SVV group, indicating that a fluid strategy targeting cardiac output augmentation through a lower SVV threshold better preserves cerebral perfusion and reduces neuronal injury markers than a more restrictive high-threshold protocol

Study Design: Secondary analysis of a randomized placebo-controlled trial
Tumor Type: Frontotemporal supratentorial brain tumors, mainly glioma and meningioma
Surgical Procedure: Elective craniotomy under general anesthesia. Original trial compared intraoperative dexmedetomidine versus placebo for delirium prevention
Mechanistic Domain(s) Addressed: Perioperative brain injury. Neurovascular unit disruption
Hemodynamic Measurements: Continuous intraoperative mean arterial pressure extracted from an anesthesia information management system, analyzed for duration, area under the curve, and time-weighted average below thresholds of 60, 65, and 70 mmHg
Neuropsychological Tests: Mini-Mental State Examination administered preoperatively and used as a baseline covariate and risk factor in the delirium model (MMSE above 26 associated with lower delirium risk)
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Delirium occurring within the first 5 postoperative days, assessed with the Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU or the 3-minute Diagnostic interview for the Confusion Assessment Method depending on setting
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Twice daily assessment for 5 postoperative days by blinded investigators, combined with Richmond Agitation Sedation Scale screening
Key Findings: 35 percent of patients experienced postoperative delirium. A data-driven threshold analysis identified 65 mmHg as the relevant hypotension cutoff, but neither unadjusted nor adjusted logistic regression found a significant association between duration, area, or time-weighted average of mean arterial pressure below 65 mmHg and postoperative delirium. Independent risk factors for delirium in the adjusted model were a preoperative Mini-Mental State Examination score above 26 (protective), intraoperative dexmedetomidine infusion (protective), history of hypertension, older age, and glioma tumor type, while intraoperative hypotension itself was not an independent predictor in this cohort with tightly controlled blood pressure management

Tumor Type: Intracerebral tumors, benign and malignant, distinguished by contrast-enhanced ultrasound
Surgical Procedure: Tumor resection with intraoperative dexmedetomidine (0.4 microgram per kilogram per hour) versus normal saline control. Tumor characterized preoperatively by contrast-enhanced ultrasound with curve-fitting time-intensity analysis
Imaging Modality: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound with time-intensity curve fitting to distinguish benign from malignant lesions preoperatively
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Serum S100 beta, neuron specific enolase, glial fibrillary acidic protein, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor alpha
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: S100 beta, NSE, and GFAP used as markers of neuronal and glial injury, IL-6 and TNF-alpha used as markers of systemic inflammatory response
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: 1 day before surgery, 1 day after surgery, and 3 days after surgery
Neuropsychological Tests: Cognitive Capacity Screening Examination and Montreal Cognitive Assessment
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Postoperative cognitive dysfunction defined by decline on Cognitive Capacity Screening Examination and Montreal Cognitive Assessment scores comparing preoperative and postoperative assessments
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: 1 day before surgery and 3 days after surgery
Key Findings: Contrast-enhanced ultrasound time-intensity parameters differed significantly between benign and malignant lesions, supporting its diagnostic use. Postoperative CCSE and MoCA scores were significantly higher and the incidence of postoperative cognitive dysfunction was significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than control. Serum S100 beta, NSE, and GFAP were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group 1 day after surgery, as were IL-6 and TNF-alpha, with levels converging with control by 3 days after surgery. Fasting blood glucose did not differ between groups at any timepoint, suggesting the cognitive and neuroprotective benefit of dexmedetomidine was not mediated through glycemic effects

Study Design: Single-center prospective randomized open-label blinded-endpoint trial
Tumor Type: Mixed brain tumors (meningioma, glioma, acoustic neurinoma, other)
Surgical Procedure: Craniotomy for brain tumor resection, comparing a frailty-originated early rehabilitation program (FORTITUDE, structured mobilization and daily-living-skills training starting on the day of surgery) versus standard nursing care
Frailty Indices/Clinical Scoring: Fried frailty phenotype (5 criteria, frailty defined as meeting 3 or more), assessed before admission and at discharge. Barthel Index for activities of daily living at discharge, 1 week, and 1 month after discharge
Postoperative Delirium Definition: Delirium status monitored throughout the hospital stay using the Nursing Delirium Screening Scale, covering 5 characteristics with a total score of 0 to 10, a score of 2 or more considered positive
Delirium Assessment Method/Timing: Nu-DESC assessed by two research nurses at three timepoints daily after surgery until discharge
Key Findings: The FORTITUDE group had a significantly lower incidence of postoperative delirium than the control group (15.6 percent vs 28.7 percent), a delayed onset of delirium, a significantly shorter duration of delirium, a shorter postoperative hospital stay, and higher activities-of-daily-living scores at 1 week and 1 month after discharge. Frailty status at admission did not differ between groups but frailty at discharge was significantly lower in the FORTITUDE group (19.9 percent vs 30.7 percent). Overall hospitalization costs and safety outcomes such as falls, unplanned extubation, and intracranial hemorrhage did not differ significantly between groups

Tumor Type: Insular glioma, WHO grade I to IV, including low-grade and high-grade
Surgical Procedure: Resection of insular gliomas with intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring and direct electrical stimulation brain mapping, trans-Sylvian or trans-cortical approach. 8 of 35 patients underwent awake craniotomy
Neuropsychological Tests: Extensive language battery including the Token Test for comprehension, Object Naming, Verb Naming, Face Recognition, Phonemic Fluency, Semantic Fluency, and word, non-word, and sentence repetition tasks
Neurological Deficit Definition: Language impairment defined by adjusted equivalent scores below normative cutoff on the language battery, with aphasic symptomatology defined as 2 or more pathological tests
Neurological Deficit Assessment Method/T: Preoperative, a few days postoperative, and 3-month follow-up assessment by trained neuropsychologists
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Language impairment on the neuropsychological battery defined by adjusted equivalent scores below normative cutoff, with aphasic symptomatology defined as 2 or more pathological tests
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Preoperative, a few days postoperative, and 3-month follow-up assessment by trained neuropsychologists
Key Findings: Patients with left-hemisphere insular lesions showed significantly worse language performance than right-hemisphere lesions at all timepoints, with a drop in performance a few days after surgery followed by partial recovery by 3 months. 92 percent of left-hemisphere patients had aphasic symptoms before and immediately after surgery, dropping to 44 percent at 3 months. Lesions involving the insula plus adjacent fronto-temporal networks produced more severe deficits than pure insular lesions. No significant correlation was found between preoperative tumor volume and language impairment, nor between extent of resection and postoperative language deficits, suggesting extent of resection is not itself a direct risk factor for language dysfunction in insular glioma surgery

Study Design: Single-center, prospective, randomized, assessor-blinded, placebo-controlled trial
Tumor Type: Supratentorial tumor (glioma and meningioma)
Surgical Procedure: Elective supratentorial tumor resection under general anesthesia, with systemic lidocaine (1.5 mg per kilogram bolus before induction then 2.0 mg per kilogram per hour infusion until end of surgery) versus volume-matched normal saline
Laboratory Biomarkers Used: Plasma S100B, neuron specific enolase, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor alpha
Biomarker Biological Interpretation: S100B and NSE used as brain injury-related markers, IL-6 and TNF-alpha used as pro-inflammatory markers, to test whether lidocaine's analgesic and anti-inflammatory properties translate into reduced brain injury signal and improved recovery
Timing of Biomarker Measurement: Before anesthesia induction and at end of surgery
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Not a cognitive test battery. Primary outcome was the Quality of Recovery-40 score covering physical comfort, emotional state, physical independence, psychological support, and pain domains
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: QoR-40 administered preoperatively and on postoperative day 1, 2, and 7
Key Findings: Global QoR-40 scores on postoperative day 1 and day 2 were significantly higher in the lidocaine group than control, driven by better physical comfort, emotional state, and pain domain scores. Lidocaine patients had significantly lower plasma S100B, NSE, IL-6, and TNF-alpha at end of surgery than control, consumed less remifentanil and propofol, had lower pain intensity scores through 24 hours, a lower incidence of postoperative nausea and vomiting, and a shorter postoperative hospital stay. Multiple linear regression identified age and pain intensity as factors correlated with postoperative recovery quality, and no persistent arrhythmia, convulsions, or other lidocaine-related adverse events were observed

Tumor Type: Glioma, low-grade and high-grade, mixed IDH status
Surgical Procedure: Awake surgery versus asleep surgery for glioma resection, both using intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring, with direct electrical stimulation mapping in the awake group
Imaging Modality: Volumetric T1 and T2/FLAIR MRI before and after surgery for lesion and resection cavity segmentation, and region-of-interest based lesion symptom mapping plus lesion network mapping using a resting-state functional MRI connectome atlas
Neuropsychological Tests: Attentional matrices test and Trail Making Test Part A, assessed 1 week before surgery, 1 week after surgery, and 1 month after surgery
Radiological Outcome Definition: Extent of resection of non-contrast-enhancing tumor volume calculated from pre- and post-surgery T1/FLAIR MRI segmentation. A non-contrast-enhancing extent of resection above 61 percent was the threshold associated with postoperative attentional decline, and a non-contrast-enhancing residual volume below 40 cubic centimeters was the threshold associated with longer overall survival in IDH wild-type glioblastoma
Cognitive Outcome Definition: Change in attentional matrices accuracy and Trail Making Test Part A completion time across preoperative, postoperative, and 1-month follow-up timepoints
Cognitive Assessment Method/Timing: Comprehensive neuropsychological assessment 1 week before surgery, 1 week after surgery, and 1 month after surgery
Key Findings: Attentional scores declined significantly 1 week after surgery on both tests, with complete recovery to preoperative levels by 1 month. Awake surgery was the only significant predictor of postoperative attentional decline among the clinical variables tested, and was associated with more extensive supramaximal resection of non-contrast-enhancing tumor regions, which correlated with the degree of attentional worsening. Lesion mapping showed that lesions involving the default mode network, particularly left prefrontal regions, were associated with worse postoperative attentional scores. Despite the transient attentional decline, awake surgery patients with IDH wild-type glioblastoma had significantly longer overall survival than asleep surgery patients (mean 887.73 vs 553.71 days), attributed to smaller postoperative non-contrast-enhancing residual volume

Tumor Type: Brain tumor (RANO setting)
Key Findings: Inter-observer agreement above 90% (kappa 0.35 to 0.83), median administration time 4 min (IQR 3 to 5).

Tumor Type: Brain tumors n = 30 (glioblastoma 7, meningioma 7, metastasis 9, other 7)

Key Findings: Weighted kappa 0.629 (sensation) to 0.935 (facial strength) across reported domains. Most patients (77%) were untreated at assessment, and the work came from a single center.

Key Findings: Median 27 (range 6 to 30), 32% abnormal. Lower MoCA tracked KPS (r = 0.35), age (r = 0.27), and MDASI-BT cognitive burden (r = -0.27). Providers found it feasible.

Key Findings: Mean MoCA-Ina 21.79 (SD 4.93), MMSE 23.76 (SD 4.08). Abnormal scores clustered at 7 to 9 years of education. Attention and calculation impaired in 90.9% (MMSE) and delayed recall in 90.9% (MoCA-Ina).

Key Findings: MoCA-INA mean 21.06 (SD 4.56) against MMSE 24.96 (SD 3.38), Pearson r = 0.71. MoCA-INA below 26 in 85.5%.

Key Findings: Mean score fell from 26.84 to 25.00 (Wilcoxon Z = -3.778, p < .001), mainly in visuospatial, attention, and memory domains.
